title.zh: 卷一百二十六 列傳第十三: 安童 廉希憲
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 列傳第十三: 安童 廉希憲 Volume 126 Biographies 13: Antong, Lianxixian

sentences.zh: 安童，木華黎四世孫，霸突魯長子也。

translations.literal: Antong was a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali and the eldest son of Batu.
translations.idiomatic: Antong, a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali, was the eldest son of Batu.

sentences.zh: 中統初，世祖追錄元勳，召入長宿衛，年方十三，位在百僚上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongtong era, the Shizu Emperor posthumously honored the founding merits and summoned him into the permanent palace guard; he was only thirteen, yet ranked above all officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongtong reign, Kublai posthumously recognized the founding merits of his forebears and summoned Antong into the permanent palace guard. Though only thirteen, he already stood above the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 母弘吉剌氏，昭睿皇后之姊，通籍禁中。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Hongjila Kereit clan, elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and held registered residence in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: His mother belonged to the Hongjila Kereit clan, was the elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and was registered to reside within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖一日見之，問及安童，對曰：「安童雖幼，公輔器也。

translations.literal: One day the Shizu Emperor saw her and asked about Antong; she replied, "Although Antong is young, he has the makings of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: One day Kublai saw her and inquired about Antong. She answered, "Young as Antong is, he has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「何以知之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How do you know that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「每退朝必與老成人語，未嘗狎一年少，是以知之。

translations.literal: She replied, "Whenever he leaves court he speaks with elderly men of experience and never keeps company with the young, and that is how I know."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "After every audience he talks with seasoned elders and never keeps company with the young—that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 」世祖悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was pleased.

sentences.zh: 四年，執阿里不哥黨千餘，將置之法，安童侍側，帝語之曰：「朕欲置此屬於死地，何如？

translations.literal: In the fourth year, more than a thousand followers of Ariq Böke were seized and were to be punished by law; Antong attended at his side, and the emperor said to him, "I wish to put these people to death—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, over a thousand partisans of Ariq Böke were arrested and were to be dealt with by law. Antong stood beside the throne, and the emperor said, "I mean to put these people to death. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「人各為其主，陛下甫定大難，遽以私憾殺人，將何以懷服未附。

translations.literal: He replied, "Each served his own lord. Your Majesty has only just settled a great crisis; if you kill people at once out of private resentment, how will you win over those not yet attached?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Each man served his own lord. Your Majesty has only just survived a great crisis; if you kill them now out of private resentment, how will you win over those who are not yet loyal?"

sentences.zh: 」帝驚曰：「卿年少，何從得老成語，此言正與朕意合。

translations.literal: The emperor said in surprise, "You are young—how did you come by such seasoned words? This remark is exactly in accord with my thought."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "You are young—where did you learn such seasoned counsel? This is exactly what I had in mind."

sentences.zh: 」由是深重之。

translations.literal: From this he came to value him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he held Antong in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 至元二年秋八月，拜光祿大夫、中書右丞相，增食邑至四千戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn in the second year of Zhiyuan, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, and his fief income was increased to four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in Zhiyuan 2, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, with his fief income raised to four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「今三方雖定，江南未附，臣以年少，謬膺重任，恐四方有輕朝廷心。

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "Though the three regions are now settled, the south is not yet attached. I am young and have wrongly accepted a weighty post; I fear the four quarters will look lightly on the court."
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "Though the three regions are settled, the south is not yet won. I am young and have wrongly taken a weighty post; I fear the realm will slight the court."

sentences.zh: 」帝動容有間曰：「朕思之熟矣，無以踰卿。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and after a pause said, "I have thought this through thoroughly—no one surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and, after a pause, said, "I have considered this at length—no one surpasses you."

sentences.zh: 」冬十月，召許衡至，傳旨令衡入省議事，衡以疾辭，安童即親候其館，與語良久，既還，念之不釋者累日。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he summoned Xu Heng; he transmitted an order for Heng to enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs, but Heng declined on grounds of illness, whereupon Antong personally visited his lodging and spoke with him for a long time; after returning, he could not put the matter out of his mind for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he summoned Xu Heng and ordered him to enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs. Heng declined on grounds of illness, so Antong went in person to his lodging and talked with him at length; after returning, he could not put the matter out of his mind for days.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝諭衡曰：「安童尚幼，未更事，善輔導之。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor instructed Heng, "Antong is still young and has not yet experienced affairs; guide him well."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor told Heng, "Antong is still young and inexperienced; guide him well."

sentences.zh: 汝有嘉謨，當先告之以達朕，朕將擇焉。

translations.literal: If you have excellent counsel, you should first tell him so that it may reach me, and I shall choose from it."
translations.idiomatic: If you have excellent counsel, tell him first so it may reach me, and I shall choose from it."

sentences.zh: 」衡對曰：「安童聰敏，且有執守，告以古人所言，悉能領解，臣不敢不盡心。

translations.literal: Heng replied, "Antong is intelligent and has firm principles; when told what the ancients said, he understands it all. I dare not fail to give my utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "Antong is intelligent and steadfast; when told what the ancients said, he grasps it fully. I dare not fail to give my utmost."

sentences.zh: 但慮中有人間之，則難行，外用勢力納人其中，則難行。

translations.literal: But I fear that if someone in the middle sows discord, it will be hard to carry out; if outside influence brings people in among us, it will also be hard."
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that if someone sows discord in the middle, counsel will be hard to carry out; if outside power pushes people into our midst, it will be equally hard."

sentences.zh: 臣入省之日淺，所見如此。

translations.literal: I have been in the Secretariat only a short time, and this is what I have seen."
translations.idiomatic: I have been in the Secretariat only a short time, and this is what I have observed."

sentences.zh: 」四年三月，安童奏：「內外官須用老成人，宜令儒臣姚樞等入省議事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year Antong memorialized, "For offices within and without the court, seasoned elders should be used; it is fitting to have Confucian officials such as Yao Shu enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year Antong memorialized, "Inside and outside the court, seasoned elders should be appointed; let Confucian officials such as Yao Shu enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此輩雖閑，猶當優養，其令入省議事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Though these men are at leisure, they should still be generously maintained; let them enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Though these men are at leisure, they should still be generously maintained. Have them enter the Secretariat to discuss affairs."

sentences.zh: 五年，廷臣密議立尚書省，以阿合馬領之，乃先奏以安童宜位三公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the courtiers secretly discussed establishing a Ministry of Revenue to be headed by Ahmad; they first memorialized that Antong should be placed among the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the courtiers secretly discussed establishing a Ministry of Revenue under Ahmad; they first memorialized that Antong should be made one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 事下諸儒議，商挺倡言曰：「安童，國之柱石，若為三公，是崇以虛名而實奪之權也，甚不可。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Confucian scholars for discussion; Shang Ting took the lead in saying, "Antong is a pillar of the state; if made one of the Three Dukes, that would honor him with an empty title while in fact stripping him of power—this must not be done."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Confucian scholars; Shang Ting led the discussion, saying, "Antong is a pillar of the state; to make him one of the Three Dukes would honor him with an empty title while in fact stripping him of power—this must not be done."

sentences.zh: 」衆曰然，事遂罷。

translations.literal: The assembly agreed, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 七年四月，奏曰：「臣近言：『尚書省、樞密院各令奏事，並如常制，其大政令，從臣等議定，然後上聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year he memorialized, "I recently said that the Ministry of Revenue and the Bureau of Military Affairs should each memorialize separately as in the usual regulations, and that major policies should be decided by us and then reported upward."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year he memorialized, "I recently proposed that the Ministry of Revenue and the Bureau of Military Affairs each memorialize separately under the usual regulations, and that major policies be decided by us before being reported upward."

sentences.zh: 』既得旨矣，今尚書一切徑奏，似違前旨。

translations.literal: We have already received the imperial assent; now the Ministry of Revenue memorializes on everything directly, which seems to violate the earlier instruction."
translations.idiomatic: We already have the imperial assent; now the Ministry memorializes on everything directly, which seems to violate that instruction."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「豈阿合馬以朕頗信用之，故爾專權耶。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Could it be that Ahmad, because I trust him rather much, therefore monopolizes power?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Has Ahmad monopolized power because I trust him rather too much?"

sentences.zh: 不與卿議，非是。

translations.literal: Not consulting you is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Not consulting you was wrong.

sentences.zh: 」敕如前旨。

translations.literal: An edict was issued as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the earlier procedure.

sentences.zh: 八年，陝西省臣也速迭兒建言，比因饑饉，盜賊滋橫，若不顯戮一二，無以示懲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Shaanxi provincial official Yesudier memorialized that, because of recent famine, bandits had grown numerous, and unless one or two were publicly executed there would be no warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Shaanxi provincial official Yesudier memorialized that recent famine had bred bandits, and unless one or two were publicly executed there would be no deterrent.

sentences.zh: 敕中書詳議，安童奏曰：「強、竊均死，恐非所宜，罪至死者，宜仍舊待報。

translations.literal: An order went to the Secretariat for detailed discussion; Antong memorialized, "To treat robbery by force and theft alike as capital offenses is probably not fitting; those whose crimes merit death should still await imperial confirmation as before."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was ordered to discuss the matter in detail; Antong memorialized, "Treating robbery by force and ordinary theft alike as capital crimes is probably unwise; those whose crimes merit death should still await imperial confirmation as before."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 十年春三月，奏以玉冊玉寶上皇后弘吉剌氏，以玉冊金寶立燕王為皇太子，兼中書令，判樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the tenth year he memorialized to present jade registers and jade seals to Empress Hongjila and to invest the Prince of Yan as heir apparent with jade register and golden seal, concurrently as Chancellor of the Secretariat and as administrator of Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the tenth year he memorialized to present jade registers and jade seals to Empress Hongjila and to invest the Prince of Yan as heir apparent with jade register and golden seal, concurrently Chancellor of the Secretariat and administrator of Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，帝諭安童及伯顏等曰：「近史天澤、姚樞纂定新格，朕已親覽，皆可行之典，汝等亦當一一留心參考，豈無一二可增減者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the emperor instructed Antong, Bayan, and others, "Recently Shi Tianze and Yao Shu compiled the new statutes; I have personally reviewed them, and they are all workable codes—you too should attend to them one by one and consult them; surely there are one or two points that may be added or reduced."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the emperor told Antong, Bayan, and the others, "Shi Tianze and Yao Shu have lately compiled the new statutes; I have reviewed them myself, and they are all workable codes. You too should study them carefully; surely one or two points may be added or trimmed."

sentences.zh: 」各令紀錄促議行之。

translations.literal: Each was ordered to record his views and hasten discussion for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Each was ordered to record his views and press for their implementation.

sentences.zh: 時天下待報死囚五十人，安童奏其中十三人因鬪毆殺人，餘無可疑。

translations.literal: At that time there were fifty condemned prisoners throughout the realm awaiting confirmation; Antong memorialized that thirteen of them had killed men in brawls while the rest were not doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fifty condemned prisoners throughout the realm awaited confirmation; Antong memorialized that thirteen had killed men in brawls while the rest raised no doubt.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以所奏十三人免死從軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued that the thirteen men he had memorialized about should be spared death and sent into military service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed that the thirteen men he had named should be spared death and sent into military service.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奏阿合馬蠹國害民數事；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized several matters in which Ahmad had harmed the state and injured the people;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he memorialized several instances in which Ahmad had harmed the state and injured the people;

sentences.zh: 又奏各部與大都路官多非才，乞加黜汰。

translations.literal: he also memorialized that many officials in the various ministries and in the Dadu circuit were without talent and begged that they be dismissed and culled.
translations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that many officials in the ministries and in the Dadu circuit lacked talent and asked that they be dismissed and culled.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，詔以行中書省樞密院事，從太子北平王出鎮極邊，在邊十年。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year an edict appointed him to conduct Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs affairs on campaign, to follow the heir apparent, the Prince of Yan, in garrisoning the far northern frontier, where he remained at the border for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year an edict appointed him to conduct Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs affairs on campaign and to follow the heir apparent, the Prince of Yan, in garrisoning the far northern frontier; he remained at the border for ten years.

sentences.zh: 二十一年三月，從王歸，待罪闕下，帝即召見慰勞之，頓首謝曰：「臣奉使無狀，有累聖德。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-first year he returned with the prince, waited at the palace gate to accept blame, and the emperor at once summoned him and comforted him; he bowed his head and apologized, saying, "In carrying out my commission I have been without merit and have burdened Your Majesty's sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-first year he returned with the prince, waited at the palace gate to accept blame, and the emperor summoned him at once to comfort him. He bowed his head and said, "In carrying out my commission I have been without merit and have burdened Your Majesty's sacred virtue."

sentences.zh: 」遂留寢殿，語至四鼓乃出。

translations.literal: He was then kept in the inner sleeping hall, and they talked until the fourth watch before he left.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept in the inner sleeping hall, and they talked until the fourth watch before he emerged.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，和禮霍孫罷，復拜中書右丞相，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Heluohosun was dismissed, and Antong was again appointed Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and given the additional title Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Heluohosun was dismissed, and Antong was again appointed Right Chancellor of the Secretariat with the additional title Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，右丞盧世榮敗，詔與諸儒條其所用人及所為事，悉罷之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Right Chancellor Lu Shirong was ruined; an edict ordered Antong and the Confucian scholars to list the men he had appointed and the things he had done, and all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Right Chancellor Lu Shirong fell; an edict ordered Antong and the Confucian scholars to list the men Lu had appointed and the measures he had taken, and all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十三年夏，中書奏擬漕司諸官姓名，帝曰：「如平章、右丞等，朕當親擇，餘皆卿等職也。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-third year the Secretariat memorialized proposing names for transport-office officials; the emperor said, "For posts such as Grand Councilor and Right Chancellor, I shall choose personally; the rest are your duty."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-third year the Secretariat memorialized proposing names for transport-office officials. The emperor said, "For posts such as Grand Councilor and Right Chancellor I shall choose personally; the rest are your duty."

sentences.zh: 」安童奏曰：「比聞聖意欲倚近侍為耳目，臣猥承任使，若所行非法，從其舉奏，罪之輕重，惟陛下裁處。

translations.literal: Antong memorialized, "I have lately heard that Your Majesty wishes to rely on close attendants as eyes and ears. I have undeservedly accepted this commission; if what I do is unlawful, let them memorialize against me, and let Your Majesty alone decide the severity of punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Antong memorialized, "I have lately heard that Your Majesty wishes to rely on close attendants as eyes and ears. I have undeservedly accepted this commission; if I act unlawfully, let them memorialize against me, and let Your Majesty alone decide the punishment."

sentences.zh: 今近臣乃伺隙援引非類，曰某居某官、某居某職，以所署奏目付中書施行。

translations.literal: Now close attendants seize opportunities to recommend unfit men, saying so-and-so should hold such-and-such an office, and hand the memorialized list to the Secretariat for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: But now close attendants seize opportunities to recommend unfit men, saying so-and-so should hold such-and-so an office, and hand the memorialized list to the Secretariat for implementation.

sentences.zh: 臣謂銓選之法，自有定制，其尤無事例者，臣常廢格不行，慮其黨有短臣者，幸陛下詳察。

translations.literal: I hold that the methods of selection and appointment have fixed regulations of their own; in the most exceptional cases without precedent I have often set the memorial aside and not carried it out, fearing that their faction will find fault with me—may Your Majesty examine this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that selection and appointment have fixed regulations; in the most exceptional cases without precedent I have often set the memorial aside, fearing their faction will find fault with me—may Your Majesty examine this carefully."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 今後若此者勿行，其妄奏者，即入言之。

translations.literal: Henceforth such things are not to be carried out; whoever memorializes falsely should be reported to me at once."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth such things must not be carried out; whoever memorializes falsely should be reported to me at once."

sentences.zh: 」奏徵前吏部尚書李昶，不起；

translations.literal: He memorialized to summon the former Minister of Personnel Li Chang, who did not come;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to summon the former Minister of Personnel Li Chang, who did not respond;

sentences.zh: 復奏賜田十頃。

translations.literal: he memorialized again to grant him ten qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized again to grant him ten qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，宗王乃顏叛，世祖親討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the imperial prince Nayan rebelled, and the Shizu Emperor personally campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the imperial prince Nayan rebelled, and Kublai personally campaigned and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 宗室詿誤者，命安童按問，多所平反。

translations.literal: Those of the imperial clan who had been implicated in error were ordered to be investigated by Antong, and many were exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the imperial clan who had been implicated in error were ordered investigated by Antong, and many were exonerated.

sentences.zh: 嘗退朝，自左掖門出，諸免罪者爭迎謝，或執轡扶上馬，安童毅然不顧。

translations.literal: Once when leaving court he went out through the left side gate; those who had been spared punishment crowded forward to thank him, some seizing the reins and helping him mount his horse, but Antong steadfastly paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Once after leaving court he went out through the left side gate; those who had been spared crowded forward to thank him, some seizing the reins and helping him mount, but Antong steadfastly paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 有乘間言於帝曰：「諸王雖有罪，皆帝室近親也，丞相雖尊，人臣也，何悖慢如此！

translations.literal: Someone seized an opportunity to tell the emperor, "Though the princes sinned, they are all close kin of the imperial house; though the chancellor is exalted, he is still a subject—how can he be so disrespectful!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Though the princes sinned, they are all close kin of the imperial house; though the chancellor is exalted, he is still a subject—how can he be so disrespectful!"

sentences.zh: 」帝良久曰：「汝等小人，豈知安童所為，特辱之使改過耳。

translations.literal: After a long pause the emperor said, "You petty men do not know what Antong is doing; he is deliberately humbling them so they may reform."
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor said, "You petty men do not understand Antong; he is deliberately humbling them so they may reform."

sentences.zh: 」是歲，復立尚書省，安童切諫曰：「臣力不能回天，乞不用桑哥，別相賢者，猶或不至虐民誤國。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Revenue was re-established; Antong urgently remonstrated, "My strength cannot turn heaven back; I beg that Sangge not be used, and that another worthy man be made chancellor instead—then perhaps the people will not be abused and the state will not be misled."
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue was re-established; Antong urgently remonstrated, "My strength cannot turn heaven back; I beg that Sangge not be used and that another worthy man be made chancellor—then perhaps the people will not be abused and the state will not be misled."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，見天下大權盡歸尚書，屢求退，不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, seeing that great power throughout the realm had all passed to the Ministry of Revenue, he repeatedly asked to retire but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, seeing that great power throughout the realm had passed to the Ministry of Revenue, he repeatedly asked to retire but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，罷相，仍領宿衛事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was dismissed as chancellor but still headed palace guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was dismissed as chancellor but still headed palace guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十年春正月，以疾薨于京師樂安里第，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the thirtieth year he died of illness at his residence in Leyue Lane in the capital; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the thirtieth year he died of illness at his residence in Leyue Lane in the capital at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 雨木冰三日，世祖震悼曰：「人言丞相病，朕固弗信，果喪予良弼。

translations.literal: Rain froze on the trees for three days; the Shizu Emperor was shaken with grief and said, "People said the chancellor was ill, but I truly did not believe it—and now I have indeed lost my worthy helper."
translations.idiomatic: Rain froze on the trees for three days; Kublai was shaken with grief and said, "People said the chancellor was ill, but I truly did not believe it—and now I have indeed lost my worthy helper."

sentences.zh: 」詔大臣監護喪事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered great ministers to supervise the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered great ministers to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，成宗制贈推忠同德翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、東平忠憲王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade, Emperor Chengzong posthumously enfeoffed him as Loyal and Faithful, Same in Virtue, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping, posthumous title Loyal and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dade, Emperor Chengzong posthumously enfeoffed him Loyal and Faithful, Same in Virtue, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping, posthumous title Loyal and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 碑曰開國元勳命世大臣之碑。

translations.literal: His stele was entitled Stele of the Founding Merit and World-Shaping Great Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His stele bore the title Stele of the Founding Merit and World-Shaping Great Minister.

sentences.zh: 子兀都帶。

translations.literal: His son was Wududai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wududai.

sentences.zh: 大德六年正月薨，年三十一。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dade he died at the age of thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dade 6 he died at the age of thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，制贈輸誠保德翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、東平王，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Conveying Sincerity, Preserving Virtue, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping, posthumous title Loyal and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 2 an edict posthumously enfeoffed him Conveying Sincerity, Preserving Virtue, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping, posthumous title Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子拜住，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Baizhu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baizhu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲

translations.literal: Lian Xixian
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian

sentences.zh: 廉希憲字善甫，布魯海牙子也。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian, style Shanfu, was the son of Buluhaia.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian, styled Shanfu, was the son of Buluhaia.

sentences.zh: 幼魁偉，舉止異凡兒。

translations.literal: In childhood he was outstanding in stature, and his bearing was unlike that of ordinary boys.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was tall and imposing, and his bearing was unlike that of ordinary boys.

sentences.zh: 九歲，家奴四人盜五馬逃去，既獲，時於法當死，父怒，將付有司，希憲泣諫止之，俱得免死。

translations.literal: At nine years old, four household slaves stole five horses and fled; after they were captured, by law they should have been put to death; his father was angry and was about to hand them over to the authorities, but Xixian wept and remonstrated until he stopped, and all were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: At nine, four household slaves stole five horses and fled; when captured, the law called for death. His father was furious and was about to hand them to the authorities, but Xixian wept and remonstrated until he stopped, and all were spared.

sentences.zh: 又嘗侍母居中山，有二奴醉出惡言，希憲曰：「是以我為幼也。

translations.literal: On another occasion, while attending his mother in residence at Zhongshan, two slaves came out drunk and spoke foully; Xixian said, "You take me for a child."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while attending his mother at Zhongshan, two slaves came out drunk and spoke foully. Xixian said, "You take me for a child."

sentences.zh: 」即送繫府獄，杖之。

translations.literal: He at once sent them to be bound in the prefectural prison and had them beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He had them sent at once to the prefectural prison and beaten.

sentences.zh: 皆奇其有識。

translations.literal: All marveled that he had such judgment.
translations.idiomatic: All marveled at his judgment.

sentences.zh: 世祖為皇弟，希憲年十九，得入侍，見其容止議論，恩寵殊絕。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor was still the imperial younger brother, Xixian at nineteen was able to enter attendance; seeing his bearing and discourse, the emperor favored him beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai was still the imperial younger brother, Xixian at nineteen entered his service; seeing his bearing and discourse, Kublai favored him beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 希憲篤好經史，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Xixian was devoted to the classics and histories and never put his books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian was devoted to the classics and histories and never put his books down.

sentences.zh: 一日，方讀孟子，聞召，急懷以進。

translations.literal: One day, while reading the Mencius, he heard himself summoned and hurried in with the book still in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while reading Mencius, he heard himself summoned and hurried in with the book still in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 世祖問其說，遂以性善義利仁暴之旨為對，世祖嘉之，目曰廉孟子，由是知名。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about its doctrines, and he answered with the themes of innate goodness, righteousness and profit, benevolence and cruelty; the emperor praised him and called him Master Lian, and from this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about its doctrines, and he answered with the themes of innate goodness, righteousness and profit, benevolence and cruelty. The emperor praised him and called him Master Lian, and from this he became renowned.

sentences.zh: 嘗與近臣校射世祖前，希憲腰插三矢，有欲取以射者，希憲曰：「汝以我為不能耶？

translations.literal: Once, while competing in archery before the emperor with close attendants, Xixian had three arrows at his waist; someone wished to take them to shoot, and Xixian said, "Do you think I cannot shoot?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while competing in archery before the emperor with close attendants, Xixian had three arrows at his waist. Someone wished to take them to shoot, and Xixian said, "Do you think I cannot shoot?"

sentences.zh: 但吾弓力稍弱耳。

translations.literal: But my bow is rather weak."
translations.idiomatic: But my bow is rather weak."

sentences.zh: 」左右授以勁弓，三發連中。

translations.literal: Those at his side gave him a strong bow, and three shots in succession all hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants gave him a strong bow, and three shots in succession all hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 衆驚服曰：「真文武材也。」

translations.literal: The assembly marveled and said in submission, "Truly a man of both civil and military talent."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly marveled and said, "Truly a man of both civil and military talent."

sentences.zh: 歲甲寅，世祖以京兆分地命希憲為宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the year jiayin the Shizu Emperor, on dividing the Jingzhao region, appointed Xixian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the year jiayin Kublai, on dividing the Jingzhao region, appointed Xixian Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 京兆控制隴蜀，諸王貴藩分布左右，民雜羌戎，尤號難治。

translations.literal: Jingzhao controlled Long and Shu; imperial princes and noble fiefs were distributed on every side, and the people were mixed with Qiang and Rong—it was especially called hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao controlled Long and Shu; imperial princes and noble fiefs lay on every side, and the people were mixed with Qiang and Rong—it was notoriously hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 希憲講求民病，抑強扶弱。

translations.literal: Xixian investigated the people's afflictions and restrained the strong while supporting the weak.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian investigated the people's afflictions and restrained the strong while supporting the weak.

sentences.zh: 暇日從名儒若許衡、姚樞輩諮訪治道，首請用衡提舉京兆學校，教育人材，為根本計。

translations.literal: In leisure he consulted famous Confucians such as Xu Heng and Yao Shu on the way of governance, and first requested that Heng be appointed to direct the Jingzhao schools to educate talent as a fundamental plan.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure he consulted famous Confucians such as Xu Heng and Yao Shu on governance, and first requested that Heng direct the Jingzhao schools to educate talent as a fundamental plan.

sentences.zh: 國制，為士者無隸奴籍，京兆多豪強，廢令不行。

translations.literal: By national regulation, scholars were not to be entered in slave registers; in Jingzhao powerful families were many and the abandoned order was not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: By national regulation scholars were not entered in slave registers; in Jingzhao powerful families were many and the abandoned order went unenforced.

sentences.zh: 希憲至，悉令著籍為儒。

translations.literal: When Xixian arrived, he ordered all to be entered in registers as scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Xixian arrived, he ordered all such persons entered in registers as scholars.

sentences.zh: 有民妻與卜者厭詛其夫，殺之，獄成，僚佐皆言方大旱，卜者宜減死，希憲議當伏法，已而大雨立應。

translations.literal: A man's wife, together with a diviner, cursed her husband by sorcery and killed him; when the case was closed the subordinates all said that with severe drought at hand the diviner's death should be reduced, but Xixian held that he should suffer the penalty by law; soon afterward heavy rain fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: A man's wife, with a diviner, cursed her husband by sorcery and killed him. When the case was closed the subordinates all said that with severe drought at hand the diviner's death should be reduced, but Xixian held he should suffer the penalty; soon afterward heavy rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖受命憲宗，經理河南關右，居數歲，讒者謂王府人多專擅不法，至是，命阿藍荅兒、劉太平檢覈所部，用酷吏分領其事，大開告訐。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shizu Emperor received his commission from Emperor Xianzong and administered Henan and the passes to the west, after several years slanderers said that many in the princely establishment acted on their own authority unlawfully; at this time Alandai'er and Liu Taiping were ordered to examine his domain, using harsh officials to take charge of each matter and opening wide the door to accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kublai received his commission from Emperor Xianzong and administered Henan and the passes to the west, after several years slanderers said many in the princely establishment acted unlawfully on their own authority; Alandai'er and Liu Taiping were then ordered to examine his domain, using harsh officials for each matter and opening wide the door to accusations.

sentences.zh: 希憲曰：「宣撫司事由己出，有罪固當獨任，僚屬何預。

translations.literal: Xixian said, "Affairs of the Pacification Commission issue from me; if there is guilt I should bear it alone—what have subordinates to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Xixian said, "Affairs of the Pacification Commission issue from me; if there is guilt I should bear it alone—what have subordinates to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 」及事竟，卒無獲罪者。

translations.literal: When the matter was concluded, in the end no one was found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was concluded, in the end no one was found guilty.

sentences.zh: 己未，憲宗駐蹕合州，世祖渡江取鄂州，命希憲入籍府庫。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei Emperor Xianzong halted at Hezhou; the Shizu Emperor crossed the river to take Ezhou and ordered Xixian to enter and register the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the year jiwei Emperor Xianzong halted at Hezhou; Kublai crossed the river to take Ezhou and ordered Xixian to enter and register the treasury stores.

sentences.zh: 希憲引儒生百餘，拜伏軍門，因言：「今王師渡江，凡軍中俘獲士人，宜官購遣還，以廣異恩。

translations.literal: Xixian led more than a hundred Confucian scholars, bowed prostrate at the army gate, and said, "Now that the royal army has crossed the river, all scholar-officials captured in the army should be purchased by the state and sent back, to extend exceptional grace."
translations.idiomatic: Xixian led more than a hundred Confucian scholars, bowed prostrate at the army gate, and said, "Now that the royal army has crossed the river, all scholar-officials captured in the army should be purchased by the state and sent back, to extend exceptional grace."

sentences.zh: 」世祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor praised and adopted the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai praised and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 還者五百餘人。

translations.literal: Those who returned numbered more than five hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred returned.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，訃音至，希憲啟曰：「殿下太祖嫡孫，先皇母弟，前征雲南，剋期撫定，及今南伐，率先渡江，天道可知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong died and the tidings of death arrived, Lian Xixian submitted and said, "Your Highness is the legitimate grandson of Taizu and the uterine younger brother of the late emperor; formerly in campaigning against Yunnan you pacified it within the set term, and now in the southern expedition you were first to cross the river—the Way of Heaven may be known."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong died and the news reached them, Lian Xixian urged Kublai: "Your Highness is Taizu's legitimate grandson and the late emperor's uterine younger brother. You pacified Yunnan on schedule in the earlier campaign, and in this southern expedition you were first across the river—the Mandate is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 且殿下收召才傑，悉從人望，子惠黎庶，率土歸心。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Highness has gathered outstanding talent, all in accord with people's hopes, treating the common folk as children, and the whole realm turns its heart to you.
translations.idiomatic: You have gathered outstanding men in line with public expectation, treated the people as your children, and won the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今先皇奄棄萬國，神器無主，願速還京，正大位以安天下。

translations.literal: Now the late emperor has suddenly abandoned the myriad states and the sacred vessel has no master; I pray you hurry back to the capital, take the great position, and settle all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor has suddenly left the realm without an heir to the throne. I beg you to return to the capital at once, take the throne, and bring peace to the empire.

sentences.zh: 」世祖然之，且命希憲先行，審察事變。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor agreed and moreover ordered Lian Xixian to go ahead first to examine how affairs had changed.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai agreed and ordered Lian Xixian to go on ahead and assess how the situation had shifted.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「劉太平、霍魯海在關右，渾都海在六盤，征南諸軍散處秦、蜀，太平要結諸將，其性險詐，素畏殿下英武，倘倚關中形勝，設有異謀，漸不可制，宜遣趙良弼往覘人情事宜。

translations.literal: He replied, "Liu Taiping and Boluha are in the passes to the west, Hunduhai is at Liupan, and the armies on the southern expedition are scattered through Qin and Shu. Taiping is essential in linking the generals; his nature is treacherous and he has always feared Your Highness's martial prowess. If he relies on the strategic advantages of Guanzhong and sets a contrary plot, it will gradually become uncontrollable. You should send Zhao Liangbi to observe human sentiment and how affairs stand."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Liu Taiping and Boluha hold the western passes, Hunduhai is at Liupan, and the southern expedition forces are scattered through Qin and Shu. Taiping is the linchpin among the generals—treacherous by nature and long in awe of your martial prowess. If he exploits Guanzhong's strategic position and plots rebellion, the situation will slip beyond control. Send Zhao Liangbi to gauge sentiment and the state of affairs."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥搆亂北邊，遣脫忽思發兵河朔，大肆凶暴。

translations.literal: Ariq Böke stirred rebellion on the northern frontier and sent Toghos to raise troops in Heshuo, committing great brutality.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Böke stirred up rebellion on the northern frontier and sent Toghos to raise troops in Heshuo, where they committed great atrocities.

sentences.zh: 真定名士李槃嘗奉莊聖太后命侍阿里不哥講讀，脫忽思怒槃不附己，械之，希憲訪槃於獄，言於世祖而釋之。

translations.literal: The renowned scholar of Zhending, Li Pan, had once received the command of the Empress Dowager Zhuangsheng to attend Ariq Böke for lectures and reading. Toghos, angered that Pan would not attach himself to him, put him in fetters. Lian Xixian visited Pan in prison, spoke to the Shizu Emperor, and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: The renowned scholar of Zhending, Li Pan, had once been ordered by Empress Dowager Zhuangsheng to attend Ariq Böke for instruction. Toghos, furious that Pan would not side with him, had him shackled. Lian Xixian visited Pan in prison, spoke to Kublai, and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 世祖命希憲賜膳於宗王塔察兒，希憲即以己意白王，宜首建翊戴之謀，王然之，許以身任其事。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor ordered Lian Xixian to grant provisions to the imperial prince Qachar. Lian Xixian at once disclosed his own view to the prince that he should first initiate the plan to support and raise [the throne], and the prince agreed and promised to bear the matter in person.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai ordered Lian Xixian to present provisions to Prince Qachar. Lian Xixian told the prince in his own words that he should be the first to launch the plan to support Kublai's accession; the prince agreed and pledged to take personal charge of the matter.

sentences.zh: 歸啟其言，世祖曰：「若此重事，卿何不懼之甚耶！」

translations.literal: Returning, he reported the prince's words. The Shizu Emperor said, "On such a weighty matter, why were you not more fearful!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported the prince's words. Kublai said, "On a matter this grave, why were you not more afraid!"

sentences.zh: 趙良弼還自關右，奏劉太平、霍魯海反狀，皆如希憲言。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangbi returned from the passes to the west and memorialized the signs of rebellion by Liu Taiping and Boluha, all exactly as Lian Xixian had said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangbi returned from the western passes and reported signs of rebellion by Liu Taiping and Boluha—everything exactly as Lian Xixian had predicted.

sentences.zh: 初分漢地為十道，乃併京兆、四川為一道，以希憲為宣撫使。

translations.literal: When the Han territories were first divided into ten circuits, Jingzhao and Sichuan were combined into one circuit and Lian Xixian was made Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Han territories were first divided into ten circuits, Jingzhao and Sichuan were merged into one, and Lian Xixian was appointed Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平、霍魯海聞之，乘驛急入京兆，密謀為變。

translations.literal: Taiping and Boluha heard of this, took the courier posts in haste to enter Jingzhao, and secretly plotted a revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping and Boluha heard the news, raced by courier post into Jingzhao, and secretly plotted a revolt.

sentences.zh: 後三日，希憲至，宣布詔旨，遣使安諭六盤。

translations.literal: Three days later Lian Xixian arrived, proclaimed the imperial edict, and sent envoys to reassure Liupan.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Lian Xixian arrived, proclaimed the imperial edict, and sent envoys to reassure Liupan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斷事官闊闊出遣使來告：渾都海已反，殺所遣使者朶羅台，遣人諭其黨密里火者於成都、乞台不花於青居，使各以兵來援，又多與蒙古軍奧魯官兀奴忽等金帛，盡起新軍，且約太平、霍魯海同日俱發。

translations.literal: Before long the judicial officer Kuokuochu sent envoys to report: Hunduhai had already rebelled, killed the envoy sent to him Duoluotai, and sent men to instruct his partisans Miri Qoja at Chengdu and Qitai Buhua at Qingju to each bring troops to his aid. He also gave much gold and silk to the Mongol army household officials such as Unuqu and raised all the new armies, and moreover agreed with Taiping and Boluha to rise on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the judicial officer Kuokuochu sent word that Hunduhai had rebelled, killed the envoy Duoluotai, and ordered his allies Miri Qoja at Chengdu and Qitai Buhua at Qingju to march to his aid. He lavished gold and silk on Mongol household officials such as Unuqu, mobilized every new army unit, and arranged with Taiping and Boluha to rise on the same day.

sentences.zh: 希憲得報，召僚屬謂曰：「上新即位，責任吾等，正為今日。

translations.literal: When Lian Xixian received the report, he summoned his subordinates and said, "The Emperor has newly taken the throne and charged us with responsibility—precisely for this day."
translations.idiomatic: When Lian Xixian received the report, he summoned his staff and said, "The Emperor has just acceded and entrusted us with responsibility—precisely for a moment like this."

sentences.zh: 不早為之計，殆將無及。

translations.literal: If we do not plan early, we will probably be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act now, it may soon be too late.

sentences.zh: 」遣萬戶劉黑馬、京兆治中高鵬霄、華州尹史廣，掩捕太平、霍魯海及其黨，獲之，盡得其奸謀，悉置於獄。

translations.literal: He sent the ten-thousand-household commander Liu Heima, the Jingzhao administrator Gao Pengxiao, and the Huazhou magistrate Shi Guang to seize Taiping, Boluha, and their partisans by surprise. They captured them, obtained their entire treacherous plot, and put them all in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the commander of ten thousand Liu Heima, Jingzhao administrator Gao Pengxiao, and Huazhou magistrate Shi Guang to seize Taiping, Boluha, and their followers by surprise. They captured them, uncovered the full conspiracy, and imprisoned them all.

sentences.zh: 復遣劉黑馬誅密里火者，緫帥汪惟正誅乞台不花，具以驛聞。

translations.literal: He again sent Liu Heima to execute Miri Qoja and the commander-in-chief Wang Weizheng to execute Qitai Buhua, reporting everything in full by courier post.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Liu Heima to execute Miri Qoja and commander Wang Weizheng to execute Qitai Buhua, reporting the full account by express courier.

sentences.zh: 時關中無兵備，命汪惟良將秦、鞏諸軍進六盤，惟良以未得上旨為辭，希憲即解所佩虎符銀印授之曰：「此皆身承密旨，君但辦吾事，制符已飛奏矣。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong had no military preparations. He ordered Wang Weiliang to lead the armies of Qin and Gong forward to Liupan. Weiliang declined on the ground that he had not yet received the supreme command. Lian Xixian at once removed the tiger tally and silver seal he wore and gave them to him, saying, "These all come from personally receiving secret instructions. You need only carry out my affairs—the tally of authority has already been reported by express post."
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had no troops in readiness. He ordered Wang Weiliang to lead the Qin and Gong armies toward Liupan, but Weiliang pleaded that he lacked imperial authorization. Lian Xixian removed his own tiger tally and silver seal and handed them over, saying, "I act under secret orders from the throne. Carry out my commission—the formal tally has already been reported by express courier."

sentences.zh: 」又付銀一萬五千兩，以充功賞，出庫幣製軍衣，惟良感激，遂行。

translations.literal: He also gave fifteen thousand taels of silver to supply merit rewards, took cloth from the treasury to make army clothing, and Weiliang, deeply moved, then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him fifteen thousand taels of silver for merit rewards, issued treasury cloth for army uniforms, and Weiliang, deeply moved, set out at once.

sentences.zh: 又發蜀卒更戍，及在家餘丁，推節制諸軍蒙古官八春將之，謂之曰：「君所將之衆，未經訓練，六盤兵精，勿與爭鋒，但張聲勢，使不得東，則大事濟矣。

translations.literal: He also mobilized Sichuan soldiers on rotation for garrison duty and remaining household males at home, and selected the Mongol officer Bachun, who regulated the armies, to lead them. He told him, "The troops you lead have not been trained. The Liupan forces are elite—do not contend with them in the clash of arms, but only display force so that they cannot move east, and the great affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: He also mobilized rotating Sichuan garrison troops and remaining household males, and put Mongol officer Bachun in command, telling him, "Your men are untrained and Liupan's troops are elite. Do not engage them head-on—only make a show of force to block their eastward advance, and the main objective will be achieved."

sentences.zh: 」會有詔赦至，希憲命絞太平等於獄，尸於通衢，方出迎詔，人心遂安。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict of amnesty arrived. Lian Xixian ordered Taiping and the others strangled in prison, exposed their corpses in the main thoroughfare, and only then went out to receive the edict, and popular sentiment was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty edict then arrived. Lian Xixian had Taiping and the others strangled in prison, displayed their bodies in the main street, and only then went out to receive the edict, and public sentiment settled.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使自劾停赦行刑、徵調諸軍、擅以惟良為帥等罪，帝深善之。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to impeach himself for the crimes of halting the amnesty to carry out executions, requisitioning the various armies, and on his own authority making Weiliang commander, and the Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to impeach himself for executing prisoners despite the amnesty, requisitioning troops, and appointing Weiliang commander on his own authority. The Emperor strongly approved his conduct.

sentences.zh: 曰：「經所謂行權，此其是也。

translations.literal: He said, "What the Classics call exercising expedient authority—this is it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is precisely what the Classics mean by exercising expedient authority."

sentences.zh: 」別賜金虎符，使節制諸軍，且詔曰：「朕委卿以方面之權，事當從宜，毋拘常制，坐失事機。」

translations.literal: He separately bestowed a gold tiger tally, making him regulate the various armies, and moreover issued an edict saying, "I entrust you with regional authority; affairs should follow what is fitting—do not be bound by regular regulations and sit by while opportunity is lost."
translations.idiomatic: He separately bestowed a gold tiger tally empowering him to command all forces, and issued an edict: "I entrust you with regional authority. Act as circumstances require—do not be bound by routine regulations and let the moment slip away."

sentences.zh: 西川將紐鄰奧魯官，將舉兵應渾都海，八春獲之，繫其黨五十餘人于乾州獄，送二人至京兆，請并殺之。

translations.literal: The Sichuan general Niuyin, a household official, was about to raise troops in response to Hunduhai. Bachun captured him, imprisoned more than fifty of his partisans in the Qianzhou jail, and sent two men to Jingzhao requesting that they all be executed together.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan general Niuyin, a household official, was about to raise troops for Hunduhai. Bachun captured him, imprisoned more than fifty of his followers at Qianzhou, and sent two prisoners to Jingzhao requesting their execution along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 二人自分必死，希憲謂僚佐曰：「渾都海不能乘勢東來，保無他慮。

translations.literal: The two men considered themselves certain to die. Lian Xixian told his subordinates, "Hunduhai cannot exploit the momentum to come east—there is certainly no other worry."
translations.idiomatic: The two men assumed they were doomed. Lian Xixian told his staff, "Hunduhai cannot exploit his momentum to march east—there is no further threat to worry about."

sentences.zh: 今衆志未一，猶懷反側，彼軍見其將校執囚，或別生心，為害不細。

translations.literal: Now the multitude's will is not yet unified and they still harbor wavering hearts. If that army sees its commanders and officers held as prisoners, they may take another course of mind, and the harm would not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: Popular loyalty is not yet unified and minds still waver. If that army sees its officers imprisoned, they may turn another way—the harm would be considerable.

sentences.zh: 今因其懼死，並加寬釋，使之感恩效力，就發此軍餘丁，往隸八春，上策也。

translations.literal: Now, because they fear death, grant them all lenient release, make them grateful and serve with effort, and at once send the remaining males of this army to be attached under Bachun—the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they fear death, release them all in mercy so they will serve in gratitude, and at once assign the army's remaining household males to Bachun—that is the best policy.

sentences.zh: 」初，八春既執諸校，其軍疑懼，駭亂四出，莫可禁遏，及知諸校獲全，紐鄰奧魯官得釋，大喜過望。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Bachun had seized the various officers, their army was suspicious and fearful, panic spreading in all directions with none able to restrain it. When they learned the officers had been spared and Niuyin the household official was released, they rejoiced beyond all expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Bachun seized the officers, their troops panicked and scattered in all directions beyond control. When they learned the officers had been spared and Niuyin released, they rejoiced beyond all expectation.

sentences.zh: 切諭其屬出兵效力，人人感悅，八春亦釋然開悟，果得精騎數千，將與俱西。

translations.literal: He urgently instructed their subordinates to bring out the army and serve with effort; every man was moved and pleased. Bachun also felt relieved and enlightened, and in the end obtained several thousand elite horsemen and led them west together.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently ordered their men to take the field and serve; every soldier was moved and delighted. Bachun too was greatly relieved, and in the end mustered several thousand elite horsemen and marched west with them.

sentences.zh: 詔以希憲為中書右丞，行秦蜀省事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Lian Xixian Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and acting head of Qin-Shu provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Lian Xixian Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with acting authority over Qin-Shu provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 渾都海聞京兆有備，遂西渡河，趨甘州，阿藍荅兒復自和林提兵與之合，分結隴、蜀諸將，又使紐鄰兄宿敦為書招紐鄰。

translations.literal: Hunduhai heard that Jingzhao was prepared and then crossed the river west, pressing toward Ganzhou. Alandai'er again raised troops from Karakorum to join him, separately winning over the generals of Long and Shu, and also had Niuyin's elder brother Sudun write a letter to recruit Niuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Hunduhai heard Jingzhao was ready and crossed west of the river toward Ganzhou. Alandai'er again raised troops from Karakorum to join him, won over generals in Long and Shu, and had Niuyin's elder brother Sudun write to recruit Niuyin.

sentences.zh: 於是成都帥百家奴，興元忙古台，青居汪惟正、欽察，俱遣使言，人心危疑，事不可測。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Chengdu commander Baijianu, Xingyuan's Mangutai, Qingju's Wang Weizheng and Qincha all sent envoys saying that popular hearts were fearful and doubtful and affairs could not be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Chengdu commander Baijianu, Mangutai at Xingyuan, and Wang Weizheng and Qincha at Qingju all sent word that morale was fearful and uncertain and the outcome could not be predicted.

sentences.zh: 希憲遣使深諭戒之，兩川諸將素憚希憲威名，按堵從命。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian sent envoys to instruct and warn them deeply. The generals of the two Sichuan circuits had long feared Lian Xixian's formidable reputation and remained settled in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian sent envoys with stern counsel and warnings. The generals of both Sichuan circuits had long feared his reputation and held their posts in obedience.

sentences.zh: 渾都海、阿藍荅兒合軍而東，諸將失利，河右大震，西土親王執畢帖木兒輜重皆空，就食秦雍。

translations.literal: Hunduhai and Alandai'er combined their armies and moved east. The generals suffered defeat and the region west of the river was greatly shaken. The western princes' baggage trains were all emptied, and they went to seek food in Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Hunduhai and Alandai'er combined forces and marched east. Government generals were defeated and the region west of the river was thrown into turmoil. Western princes' supply trains were stripped bare, and they fled to Qin and Yong for provisions.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲棄兩川，退守興元，希憲力言不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Court deliberation wished to abandon the two Sichuan circuits and withdraw to defend Xingyuan. Lian Xixian strongly argued it could not be done, and the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated abandoning both Sichuan circuits and falling back to defend Xingyuan. Lian Xixian argued forcefully against it, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 會親王合丹及汪惟良、八春等合兵復戰西涼，大敗之，俘斬略盡，得二叛首以送，梟之京兆市。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial prince Hede, together with Wang Weiliang, Bachun, and others, combined forces and fought again at Xiliang, inflicting a great defeat; captives and slain were nearly all gone. The two rebel leaders were obtained and sent; they were exposed in the Jingzhao market.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hede, Wang Weiliang, Bachun, and others then combined forces and fought again at Xiliang, inflicting a crushing defeat that left few survivors. The two rebel leaders were captured and sent to Jingzhao, where they were displayed in the market.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝大嘉之曰：「希憲真男子也。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor greatly praised him and said, "Lian Xixian is a true man."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the Emperor praised him highly and said, "Lian Xixian is a true man."

sentences.zh: 」進拜平章政事，賜宅一區。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councillor of State and granted one residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Councillor of State and granted a residence.

sentences.zh: 時希憲年三十矣。

translations.literal: At the time Lian Xixian was thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian was then thirty years old.

sentences.zh: 希憲奏：四川降民，皆散處山谷，宜申敕軍吏，禁止俘掠，違者，千戶以下與犯人同罪。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian memorialized: The surrendered people of Sichuan are all scattered in mountain valleys. It is fitting to issue stern orders to army officers forbidding capture and plunder. Violators, down to the level of thousand-household commanders, should share the culprit's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian memorialized that Sichuan's surrendered populace were scattered in mountain valleys and urged strict orders to army officers forbidding capture and plunder, with violators down to thousand-household commanders punished equally with the culprits.

sentences.zh: 又禁諸人無販易生口，由是四川遂安，降者益衆。

translations.literal: He also forbade all persons to trade in living persons as goods. Thereby Sichuan was soon settled and those who surrendered grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade the trafficking of human captives, and Sichuan soon grew calm as ever more people surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又罷解鹽戶所摘軍，及京兆諸處無籍戶之戍靈州屯田者，以寬民力。

translations.literal: He also abolished the soldiers drafted from salt households and those from households without registers in various places around Jingzhao who garrisoned Lingzhou for frontier farming, to ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also ended conscription of salt-household troops and the garrison farming duty at Lingzhou imposed on unregistered households around Jingzhao, to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 欽察獲宋臣張炳震、王政二人，俱以母老，願賜矜放，希憲皆遣之還。

translations.literal: Qincha captured the Song officials Zhang Bingzhen and Wang Zheng. Both, on the ground that their mothers were old, asked to be granted compassionate release. Lian Xixian sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: Qincha captured the Song officials Zhang Bingzhen and Wang Zheng. Both pleaded that their mothers were elderly and asked for compassionate release. Lian Xixian sent them home.

sentences.zh: 因為書與宋四川制置余玠，諭以天道人事，玠得書愧感自守，不敢復輕動。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote a letter to the Song Sichuan commissioner Yu Jie, instructing him on the Way of Heaven and human affairs. When Jie received the letter he felt shame and gratitude and held himself in check, not daring to act lightly again.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to the Song Sichuan commissioner Yu Jie, instructing him on Heaven's mandate and human affairs. Jie, shamed and moved by the letter, held his position and dared not stir again.

sentences.zh: 鞏昌帥府言，鎮戎州有謀為叛者，連引四百餘人，希憲詳推之，惟誅首惡五人。

translations.literal: The Gongchang commandery reported that at Zhenrong Prefecture there were plotters of rebellion, implicating in succession more than four hundred persons. Lian Xixian examined the case in detail and executed only the five chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongchang command reported a conspiracy at Zhenrong Prefecture that implicated more than four hundred people. Lian Xixian investigated thoroughly and executed only the five ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 宋將劉整以瀘州降，盡繫前歸宋者數百人待報。

translations.literal: The Song general Liu Zheng surrendered Luzhou. Several hundred who had earlier gone over to the Song were all imprisoned awaiting report.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Liu Zheng surrendered Luzhou. Several hundred men who had earlier defected to the Song were imprisoned pending orders.

sentences.zh: 希憲奏釋之，且致書宰臣，待整以恩，當得其死力。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian memorialized to release them and moreover sent a letter to the chief ministers, saying that if Zheng were treated with grace, one would surely obtain his utmost loyal service unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian memorialized for their release and wrote the chief ministers that if Liu Zheng were treated with grace, he would serve with his utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 整後首建取襄陽之策，果立勳效。

translations.literal: Zheng later was first to propose the plan to take Xiangyang and indeed established meritorious achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng later was the first to propose taking Xiangyang and indeed won great distinction.

sentences.zh: 宋將家屬之在北者，希憲歲給其糧，仕於宋者，子弟得越界省其親，人皆感之。

translations.literal: For the families of Song generals who were in the north, Lian Xixian yearly supplied their grain. For those serving in the Song, their sons and younger brothers were able to cross the border to visit their kin, and all were moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: For Song generals' families held in the north, Lian Xixian supplied grain each year. For those serving the Song, their sons and brothers were allowed to cross the border to visit kin, and all were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 李璮反山東，事連王文統，平章趙璧素忌希憲勳名，因言文統由張易、希憲薦引，遂至大用，且關中形勝之地，希憲得民心，有商挺、趙良弼為之輔，此事宜關聖慮。

translations.literal: Li Tan rebelled in Shandong and the affair implicated Wang Wentong. The Grand Councillor Zhao Bi had long resented Lian Xixian's merit and fame and therefore said that Wentong had been recommended and introduced by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian and thus came to great employment, and moreover that in the strategically advantageous land of Guanzhong Lian Xixian had won the people's hearts, with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his assistants—this matter should concern the sage's consideration.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled in Shandong, the affair implicated Wang Wentong. Grand Councillor Zhao Bi, who had long resented Lian Xixian's fame, said Wentong had risen through recommendations by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian, that Lian Xixian held the strategic Guanzhong region and had won popular loyalty with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his aides—matters that should concern the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「希憲自幼事朕，朕知其心，挺、良弼皆正士，何慮焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」蜀降人費正寅以私怨譖希憲因李璮叛，亦修城治兵，潛畜異志，帝因惑之，命中書右丞南合代希憲行省，且覆視所告事，卒無實狀。

translations.literal: A surrendered man of Shu, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private resentment, saying that because of Li Tan's rebellion he too was repairing walls and training troops and secretly harbored a contrary intent. The Emperor was thereby misled and ordered the Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Nanhe to replace Lian Xixian in provincial administration and moreover reinvestigate the reported matters. In the end there was no substantiating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: A surrendered Shu man, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private spite, claiming that amid Li Tan's rebellion he too was fortifying cities, drilling troops, and harboring secret ambitions. The Emperor was unsettled and ordered Right Vice Director Nanhe to replace him in provincial administration and reinvestigate the charges. In the end nothing was substantiated.

sentences.zh: 詔希憲還京師，陛見，言曰：「方關陝叛亂，川蜀未寧，事急星火，臣隨宜行事，不謀佐貳，如寅所言，罪止在臣，臣請逮繫有司。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lian Xixian back to the capital. At audience he said, "Just when Guan and Shaan were in rebellion and Chuan and Shu were not yet settled, affairs were urgent as sparks and fire. Your servant acted as circumstances required without consulting a second adviser. As Zhengyin said, guilt rests only on your servant. I request to be seized and handed to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Lian Xixian to the capital. At audience he said, "When Guan-Shaan was in rebellion and Sichuan unsettled, affairs were urgent as fire. I acted as circumstances required without consulting colleagues. If Zhengyin's charges hold, guilt rests on me alone—I ask to be handed over to the authorities."

sentences.zh: 」帝撫御床曰：「當時之言，天知之，朕知之，卿果何罪！

translations.literal: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "What was said at the time—Heaven knows it, I know it—what crime do you truly have!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "Heaven knows what you did then, and so do I—what crime have you truly committed!"

sentences.zh: 」慰諭良久。

translations.literal: He comforted and instructed him at length.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted and reassured him at length.

sentences.zh: 進拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 一日夜半，召希憲入禁中，從容道藩邸時事，因及趙璧所言。

translations.literal: One day at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs in the princely establishment, and thereby touched on what Zhao Bi had said.
translations.idiomatic: One night at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs from the princely years, and brought up what Zhao Bi had said.

sentences.zh: 希憲曰：「昔攻鄂時，賈似道作木柵環城，一夕而成，陛下顧扈從諸臣曰『吾安得如似道者用之』。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian said, "In the past when attacking Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades encircling the city wall, completed in a single night. Your Majesty turned to the various ministers in attendance and said, 'How might I obtain and employ someone like Sidao?'"
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian said, "During the attack on Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades around the city wall in a single night. Your Majesty turned to your attendants and said, 'How might I find and employ someone like Sidao?'"

sentences.zh: 劉秉忠、張易進曰『山東王文統，才智士也。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi advanced and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi stepped forward and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'

sentences.zh: 今為李璮幕僚』。

translations.literal: He is now a staff officer of Li Tan.'
translations.idiomatic: He is now on Li Tan's staff.'

sentences.zh: 詔問臣，臣對『亦聞之，實未嘗識其人也』。

translations.literal: Your Majesty questioned your servant, and your servant replied, 'I too have heard of him, but in truth I have never known the man.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty asked me, and I replied, 'I too have heard of him, but I have never actually known the man.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕亦記此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I too remember this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I remember that as well."

sentences.zh: 希憲在中書，振舉綱維，綜劾名實，汰逐冗濫，裁抑僥倖，興利除害，事無不便，當時翕然稱治，典章文物，粲然可考。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat Lian Xixian raised the governing framework, examined names against realities, eliminated the redundant and excessive, restrained opportunistic favor, advanced benefit and removed harm—there was nothing not made fitting. At the time all together praised good order, and institutions and cultural objects shone forth and could be verified.
translations.idiomatic: At the Secretariat Lian Xixian revived governance, matched names to realities, purged redundancy, curbed opportunism, and advanced the public good—nothing was left ill served. The age hailed his rule, and institutions and cultural standards shone forth for all to see.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「國家自開創已來，凡納土及始命之臣，咸令世守，至今將六十年，子孫皆奴視部下，都邑長吏，皆其皂隸僮使，前古所無，宜更張之，使考課黜陟。

translations.literal: He also proposed: "Since the state's founding, all who surrendered territory and ministers first appointed have been ordered to hold their posts in perpetuity. Down to today it is nearly sixty years. Their descendants all treat subordinates as slaves, and prefectural and district chief officials are all their menial servants and attendants—something without precedent in antiquity. It is fitting to change and expand this, instituting examination for promotion and demotion."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that since the founding, surrendered territories and first-appointed ministers had held hereditary posts for nearly sixty years, their descendants treating subordinates as slaves and local officials as personal servants—unprecedented in history—and urged reform with examination-based promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: 」始議行遷轉法。

translations.literal: Discussion first began on implementing the rotation law.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion then began on instituting a rotation system for officials.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，丁母憂，率親族行古喪禮，勺飲不入口者三日，慟則嘔血，不能起，寢卧草土，廬于墓傍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he entered mourning for his mother, led his kin in performing the ancient mourning rites, and for three days took not a spoonful of drink into his mouth. When he grieved he vomited blood, could not rise, slept on grass and earth, and built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he mourned his mother, led his kin in ancient funeral rites, and for three days took no food or drink. Grief brought him to vomiting blood; he could not rise, slept on bare earth, and built a mourning hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 宰執以憂制未定，欲極力起之，相與詣廬，聞號痛聲，竟不忍言。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, because the mourning regulations were not yet settled, wished to exert all effort to raise him from mourning. They went together to the hut, heard the sounds of wailing and pain, and in the end could not bear to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, with mourning regulations still unsettled, wished to recall him to office and went together to the mourning hut. Hearing his cries of grief, they could not bring themselves to speak.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有詔奪情起復，希憲雖不敢違旨，然出則素服從事，入必縗絰。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict to seize feeling and recall him to service. Lian Xixian, though he did not dare disobey the command, when he went out wore plain mourning garments while conducting affairs, and when he entered always wore the hemp mourning bands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him recalled from mourning to office. Though he dared not disobey, he wore plain mourning dress when he went out to work and full mourning garb whenever he returned home.

sentences.zh: 及喪父，亦如之。

translations.literal: When he mourned his father, he did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he did the same.

sentences.zh: 奸臣阿合馬領左右部，專緫財賦，會其黨相攻擊，帝命中書推覆，衆畏其權，莫敢問。

translations.literal: The treacherous minister Ahmad headed the Left and Right Offices and exclusively oversaw finances and taxes. It happened that his faction attacked one another. The Emperor ordered the Secretariat to investigate and verify, but all feared his power and none dared inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt minister Ahmad headed the Left and Right Offices and controlled finances. When his faction turned on one another, the Emperor ordered the Secretariat to investigate, but all feared his power and none dared pursue the case.

sentences.zh: 希憲窮治其事，以狀聞，杖阿合馬，罷所領歸有司。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian exhaustively prosecuted the affair, reported the facts, had Ahmad beaten with the staff, and abolished what he oversaw, returning it to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian prosecuted the case to the end, reported the findings, had Ahmad beaten with the staff, and stripped him of his offices, returning their functions to the regular bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 帝諭希憲曰：「吏廢法而貪，民失業而逃，工不給用，財不贍費，先朝患此久矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Lian Xixian, saying, "Officials abandon the law and are greedy; the people lose their occupations and flee; craftsmen do not supply what is needed; finances do not meet expenditures—the previous court suffered from this for long."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Lian Xixian, "Officials abandon the law and grow greedy; the people lose their livelihoods and flee; craftsmen cannot meet demand; revenues cannot cover expenses—the previous reign suffered from this for years."

sentences.zh: 自卿等為相，朕無此憂。

translations.literal: Since you and the others became chancellors, I have had no such worry.
translations.idiomatic: Since you and the others became chancellors, I have had no such worry.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下聖猶堯、舜，臣等未能以皋陶、稷、契之道，贊輔治化，以致太平，懷愧多矣。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's sagacity is like that of Yao and Shun, yet your servants have been unable with the Way of Gao Yao, Ji, and Qi to assist and support the transformation of governance and bring about great peace—we harbor much shame."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty's sagacity equals Yao and Shun's, yet we have failed to assist your rule with the wisdom of Gao Yao, Ji, and Qi and bring true peace—we are deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 今日小治，未足多也。

translations.literal: Today's slight order is not enough to boast of.
translations.idiomatic: Today's modest order is hardly worth boasting of.

sentences.zh: 」因論及魏徵，對曰：「忠臣良臣，何代無之，顧人主用不用爾。

translations.literal: Thereupon they discussed Wei Zheng. He replied, "Loyal ministers and good ministers—what age lacks them? It only depends on whether the ruler employs them or not."
translations.idiomatic: They then spoke of Wei Zheng. He replied, "Loyal and worthy ministers exist in every age—it only depends on whether the ruler uses them."

sentences.zh: 」有內侍傳旨入朝堂，言某事當爾，希憲曰：「此閹宦預政之漸，不可啟也。

translations.literal: A palace attendant transmitted an order into the court hall, saying a certain matter should be thus. Lian Xixian said, "This is the first step of eunuchs intervening in government—it must not be opened."
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant brought an order into court saying a certain matter should be handled thus. Lian Xixian said, "This is the first step toward eunuchs meddling in government—it must not be allowed."

sentences.zh: 」遂入奏，杖之。

translations.literal: He then entered to memorialize and had him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne and had the attendant beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 言者訟丞相史天澤，親黨布列中外，威權日盛，漸不可制。

translations.literal: Accusers sued the Chancellor Shi Tianze, saying his kin and partisans were deployed throughout court and countryside, his authority and power growing daily, gradually beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers charged Chancellor Shi Tianze with deploying kin and allies throughout the realm, his power growing daily until it was becoming ungovernable.

sentences.zh: 詔罷天澤政事，使待鞫問。

translations.literal: An edict removed Tianze from governmental affairs and made him await interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Tianze from office and ordered him held pending interrogation.

sentences.zh: 希憲進曰：「天澤事陛下久，知天澤深者，無如陛下。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian advanced and said, "Tianze has served Your Majesty for long. None knows Tianze deeply like Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian stepped forward and said, "Tianze has served Your Majesty for many years. No one knows him as well as you do."

sentences.zh: 始自潛藩，多經任使，將兵牧民，悉有治效。

translations.literal: From the beginning in the hidden princely establishment he passed through many appointments; leading troops and governing the people, all had governing effect.
translations.idiomatic: From your princely years he held many posts; whether leading troops or governing the people, he achieved real results.

sentences.zh: 陛下知其可付大事，用為輔相，小人一旦有言，陛下當熟察其心跡，果有肆橫不臣者乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty knew he could be entrusted with great affairs and employed him as assisting minister. When petty men suddenly have words, Your Majesty should carefully examine his heart and traces—is there truly one who acts wildly and disloyally?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knew he could bear great responsibility and made him chancellor. When petty men speak against him, you should examine his conduct carefully—is there truly any sign of arrogance or disloyalty?

sentences.zh: 今日信臣，故臣得預此旨，他日有訟臣者，臣亦遭疑矣。

translations.literal: Today Your Majesty trusts your servant, and therefore your servant may share in this command. Another day, if there are accusers of your servant, your servant too will meet with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Today you trust me, so I may speak thus. Another day, if someone accuses me, I too will fall under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 臣等備員政府，陛下之疑信若此，何敢自保。

translations.literal: Your servants fill posts in government. If Your Majesty's doubt and trust are like this, how dare we preserve ourselves?
translations.idiomatic: We merely fill posts in your government. If your trust and doubt swing like this, how can any of us feel secure?

sentences.zh: 天澤既罷，亦當罷臣。

translations.literal: Since Tianze has already been removed, your servant too should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If Tianze is removed, I should be removed as well.

sentences.zh: 」帝良久曰：「卿且退，朕思之。
