translations.literal: After a long while the Emperor said, "Withdraw for now—I will think on it."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the Emperor said, "Withdraw for now—I will consider it."

sentences.zh: 」明日，帝召希憲諭曰：「昨思之，天澤無對訟者。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned Lian Xixian and instructed him, saying, "Yesterday I thought on it—Tianze has no accuser to face in suit."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor summoned Lian Xixian and said, "I thought it over—no one has come forward to substantiate the charges against Tianze."

sentences.zh: 」事遂解。

translations.literal: The affair was thereby resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又有訟四川帥欽察者，帝敕中書急遣使誅之。

translations.literal: There were again accusers of the Sichuan commander Qincha. The Emperor commanded the Secretariat urgently to send envoys to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers again charged the Sichuan commander Qincha. The Emperor ordered the Secretariat to send envoys at once to execute him.

sentences.zh: 明日，希憲覆奏，帝怒曰：「尚爾遲回耶！

translations.literal: The next day Lian Xixian submitted a follow-up memorial. The Emperor angrily said, "Still so hesitant!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lian Xixian submitted a follow-up memorial. The Emperor said angrily, "Still dragging your feet!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「欽察大帥，以一小人言被誅，民心必駭，收繫至此，與訟者廷對，然後明其罪於天下為宜。

translations.literal: He replied, "Qincha is a great commander. To be executed on the word of a petty man will surely terrify popular hearts. It is fitting to seize and bring him here, confront him in court with the accusers, and only then clarify his guilt before all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Qincha is a senior commander. To execute him on a petty man's word will terrify the people. Bring him here, confront him in court with his accusers, and only then make his guilt clear to the realm—that is the proper course."

sentences.zh: 」詔遣能者按問，其後事竟無實，欽察得免。

translations.literal: An edict sent capable men to investigate and question. Afterward the affair in the end had no substance, and Qincha was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent capable investigators. The charges proved baseless, and Qincha was spared.

sentences.zh: 希憲每奏議帝前，論事激切，無少回惜。

translations.literal: Whenever Lian Xixian memorialized and deliberated before the Emperor, he discussed affairs with fierce urgency and not the least holding back.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Lian Xixian addressed the throne, he spoke with fierce urgency and never held back.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿昔事朕王府，多所容受，今為天子臣，乃爾木強耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "In the past when you served me in the princely establishment you were much indulged and accepted. Now as the Son of Heaven's minister, are you thus so stubborn and unyielding?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When you served me in the princely household I indulged you often. Now that you are the Son of Heaven's minister, have you become so stubborn?"

sentences.zh: 」希憲對曰：「王府事輕，天下事重，一或面從，天下將受其害，臣非不自愛也。」

translations.literal: Lian Xixian replied, "Affairs of the princely establishment were light; affairs of all under Heaven are heavy. If once I agree to your face, all under Heaven will suffer the harm. Your servant is not without self-regard."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian replied, "Princely affairs were light; the affairs of the empire are heavy. If I once agreed to your face for convenience, the realm would suffer—and I am not without regard for my own safety."

sentences.zh: 方士請煉大丹，敕中書給所需，希憲具以秦、漢故事奏，且曰：「堯、舜得壽，不因大丹也。

translations.literal: Daoist masters requested to refine the great elixir pill. An edict ordered the Secretariat to supply what was needed. Lian Xixian fully presented Qin and Han precedents in memorial and said, "Yao and Shun attained longevity—not because of the great elixir."
translations.idiomatic: Daoist alchemists asked to refine the great elixir of immortality, and Kublai ordered the Secretariat to provide whatever they needed. Lian Xixian memorialized the throne at length with Qin and Han precedents and said, "Yao and Shun lived long lives without any such pill."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is so."

sentences.zh: 」遂却之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 時方尊禮國師，帝命希憲受戒，對曰：「臣受孔子戒矣。

translations.literal: At the time they were honoring the State Preceptor. The Emperor ordered Lian Xixian to receive precepts. He replied, "Your servant has received Confucius's precepts."
translations.idiomatic: The court was then honoring the State Preceptor, and Kublai ordered Lian Xixian to take Buddhist vows. He replied, "Your servant has already taken Confucius's vows."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「孔子亦有戒耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Does Confucius also have precepts?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Does Confucius have vows too?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「為臣當忠，為子當孝，孔子之戒，如是而已。」

translations.literal: He replied, "As minister one should be loyal; as son one should be filial—Confucius's precepts are no more than this."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "A minister should be loyal; a son should be filial—that is all there is to Confucius's vows."

sentences.zh: 五年，始建御史臺，繼設各道提刑按察司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Censorate was first established, followed by establishing the circuit offices for criminal investigation and surveillance in each route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of his reign, Kublai established the Censorate and then set up circuit offices for criminal investigation and surveillance in every province.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬專緫財利，乃曰：「庶務責成諸路，錢穀付之轉運，今繩治之如此，事何由辦？

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad monopolized control of revenue and profit. He said, "Miscellaneous affairs are entrusted to the various routes; grain and funds are given to the transport commissioners—now to restrain and govern like this, how can affairs be accomplished?"
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad then controlled the finances single-handedly and objected: "Routine administration is left to the provinces, and grain and revenue to the transport offices—if you tie our hands like this, how is anything supposed to get done?"

sentences.zh: 」希憲曰：「立臺察，古制也，內則彈劾奸邪，外則察視非常，訪求民瘼，裨益國政，無大於此。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian said, "Establishing the surveillance commissioners is an ancient institution—inwardly they impeach the wicked and depraved, outwardly they inspect anomalies, seek out the people's afflictions, and benefit state policy—nothing is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian replied, "Surveillance offices are an ancient institution: within the court they impeach the corrupt; beyond it they watch for irregularities, seek out the people's grievances, and strengthen the state. Nothing matters more."

sentences.zh: 若去之，使上下專恣貪暴，事豈可集耶！

translations.literal: If removed, letting those above and below indulge exclusively in greed and violence—how can affairs be brought together?
translations.idiomatic: Remove them, and those above and below will give themselves wholly to greed and violence—how then can the state function at all?"

sentences.zh: 」阿合馬不能對。

translations.literal: Ahmad could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad had no answer.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔釋京師繫囚。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict released prisoners held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict ordered the release of prisoners held in the capital.

sentences.zh: 西域人匿贊馬丁，用事先朝，資累鉅萬，為怨家所告，繫大都獄，既釋之矣，時希憲在告，實不預其事。

translations.literal: A Western Region man, Nazr al-Din, employed in service of the previous court, with assets accumulated to tens of millions, was denounced by an enemy family and imprisoned in the Dadu jail. He had already been released. At the time Lian Xixian was on leave and truly did not participate in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A Central Asian named Nazr al-Din, who had served the previous regime and amassed a fortune, was denounced by an enemy and imprisoned in Dadu; he had already been released. Lian Xixian was on leave at the time and had nothing to do with the decision.

sentences.zh: 是秋，車駕還自上都，怨家訴於帝，希憲取堂判補署之，曰：「天威莫測，豈可幸其獨不署以苟免耶。

translations.literal: That autumn, when the imperial carriage returned from Shangdu, the enemy family appealed to the Emperor. Lian Xixian took the hall decision and added his signature, saying, "Heaven's majesty cannot be measured—how can one hope that alone by not signing one might escape?"
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the imperial procession returned from Shangdu, the accuser appealed to Kublai. Lian Xixian found the court order and signed it, saying, "The Emperor's will is unpredictable—how could I gamble on being the one official who had not signed and hope to escape blame?"

sentences.zh: 」希憲入見，以詔書為言，帝曰：「詔釋囚耳，豈有詔釋匿贊馬丁耶？

translations.literal: Lian Xixian entered audience and spoke in terms of the edict. The Emperor said, "The edict releases prisoners—was there an edict releasing Nazr al-Din?"
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian went in to see him and cited the edict. Kublai said, "The edict was to release prisoners in general—when did it order the release of Nazr al-Din?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不釋匿贊馬丁，臣等亦未聞有此詔。

translations.literal: He replied, "In not releasing Nazr al-Din, your servants likewise had not heard of such an edict."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If Nazr al-Din was not to be released, then we too had never heard of any such edict."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「汝等號稱讀書，臨事乃爾，宜得何罪？

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said, "You call yourselves readers of books—facing affairs you are thus—what crime should you receive?"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said angrily, "You style yourselves scholars, yet this is how you handle affairs—what punishment do you deserve?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣等忝為宰相，有罪當罷退。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servants are ashamed to stand as chancellors; if guilty we should be dismissed and removed."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "We are unworthy to serve as chancellors; if we are guilty, we should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「但從汝言。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Simply follow your words."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Very well—do as you say."

sentences.zh: 」即與左丞相耶律鑄同罷。

translations.literal: Immediately he was removed together with Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed at once, together with the left chancellor Yelü Zhu.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝問侍臣，希憲居家何為，侍臣以讀書對。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor asked the attending ministers what Lian Xixian did at home. The ministers answered that he read books.
translations.idiomatic: One day Kublai asked his attendants what Lian Xixian did at home. They said he spent his time reading.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「讀書固朕所教，然讀之而不肯用，多讀何為。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Reading books is indeed what I taught—but to read and yet be unwilling to use them—what is the use of much reading?"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "I am the one who taught him to read—but what is the point of reading if he will not put what he learns to use?"

sentences.zh: 」意責其罷政而不復求進也。

translations.literal: The meaning was to blame him for leaving office and not seeking advancement again.
translations.idiomatic: The remark was meant to reproach him for leaving office and not seeking to return.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬因讒之曰：「希憲日與妻子宴樂爾。

translations.literal: Ahmad therefore slandered him, saying, "Lian Xixian daily feasts and enjoys himself with wife and children—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad seized the moment to slander him: "Lian Xixian spends his days feasting with his wife and children, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」帝變色曰：「希憲清貧，何從宴設。

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said, "Lian Xixian is pure and poor—whence would banquets come?"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai's expression darkened. "Lian Xixian is poor and austere—where would he find the means for feasting?"

sentences.zh: 」希憲嘗有疾，帝遣醫三人診視，醫言須用沙糖作飲，時最艱得，家人求於外，阿合馬與之二斤，且致密意。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian had once been ill. The Emperor sent three physicians to examine him. The physicians said rock sugar must be used to make a drink; at the time it was hardest to obtain. The family sought it outside; Ahmad gave them two jin and moreover conveyed intimate regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian Xixian fell ill, Kublai sent three physicians. They prescribed a drink made with rock sugar, which was then almost impossible to find. His household searched outside the home; Ahmad gave them two jin and sent his regards with the gift.

sentences.zh: 希憲却之曰：「使此物果能活人，吾終不以奸人所與求活也。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian refused it, saying, "Suppose this substance truly could save a life—I would still never seek life from what a villain gave."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian refused it, saying, "Even if this could truly save my life, I would never buy my survival with a villain's gift."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞而遣賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and sent it as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai heard of this, he sent the sugar as an imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 嗣國王頭輦哥行省鎮遼陽，有言其擾民不便者。

translations.literal: The heir king Toulenko governed Liaoyang as pacification commissioner. There were reports that he disturbed the people and it was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The heir king Toulenko was governing Liaoyang as regional commissioner, and there were complaints that his administration was oppressing the people.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔起希憲為北京行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict recalled Lian Xixian as Pacification Commissioner of the Beijing Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, an edict recalled Lian Xixian and appointed him Pacification Commissioner of the Beijing Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將行，肩輿入辭，賜坐，帝曰：「昔在先朝，卿深識事機，每以帝道啟朕，及鄂漢班師，屢陳天命，朕心不忘，丞相卿實宜為，顧退托耳。

translations.literal: About to depart, he entered in a sedan chair to take leave; granted a seat. The Emperor said, "In the past during the former reign you deeply understood affairs; each time you opened me to the Way of the Emperor; when the army withdrew from Ezhou and Hankou you repeatedly stated Heaven's mandate—I have not forgotten in my heart. Chancellor—you truly should hold the post, only you declined on pretext."
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, he came to take leave in a sedan chair and was given a seat. Kublai said, "In my princely days you understood affairs deeply and always set me on the path of kingship; when our forces withdrew from Ezhou and Hankou you spoke again and again of Heaven's mandate, and I have never forgotten. You were truly fit to be chancellor—you only declined on one pretext or another."

sentences.zh: 遼霫戶不下數萬，諸王、國壻分地所在，彼皆素知卿能，故命卿往鎮，體朕此意。

translations.literal: Liaoyang and Mohe households number no fewer than tens of thousands; wherever princes and imperial sons-in-law have divided lands, they all long knew your ability—therefore I order you to go to govern; embody this intent of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang and the Mohe lands have tens of thousands of households, and wherever princes and imperial sons-in-law hold fiefs they have long known your abilities. That is why I send you to govern there—carry out my intent."

sentences.zh: 」遼東多親王，使者傳令旨，官吏立聽，希憲至，始革正之。

translations.literal: Liaodong has many imperial princes; envoys transmitted imperial orders and officials stood to listen. When Lian Xixian arrived, only then was this reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong had many imperial princes whose envoys delivered orders while officials stood at attention to hear them. Only after Lian Xixian arrived was that practice corrected.

sentences.zh: 有西域人自稱駙馬，營于城外，繫富民，誣其祖父嘗貸息錢，索償甚急，民訴之行省，希憲命收捕之。

translations.literal: A Western Region man styled himself imperial son-in-law, encamped outside the city, seized a wealthy commoner, falsely charged that his grandfather once lent interest money, and demanded repayment urgently. The people appealed to the Branch Secretariat; Lian Xixian ordered him seized.
translations.idiomatic: A Central Asian who called himself an imperial son-in-law camped outside the city, seized a wealthy man, and falsely claimed his grandfather had once lent money at interest, demanding repayment at once. The victim appealed to the regional government, and Lian Xixian ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 其人怒，乘馬入省堂，坐榻上，希憲命捽下跪，而問之曰：「法無私獄，汝何人，敢擅繫民？

translations.literal: That man was angry, rode a horse into the secretariat hall, and sat on the couch. Lian Xixian ordered him seized and kneeling, then questioned him: "The law has no private jails—you—what person are you, daring to detain people on your own authority?"
translations.idiomatic: The man stormed in on horseback, entered the hall, and sat on the dais. Lian Xixian had him seized and forced to his knees, then demanded: "The law permits no private prisons—who are you to detain subjects on your own authority?"

sentences.zh: 」令械繫之。

translations.literal: He ordered him shackled and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him shackled and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 其人惶懼求哀，國王亦為之請，乃稍寬，令待對，舉營夜遁。

translations.literal: That man fearfully begged for mercy; the king also pleaded for him—then slightly lenient, ordered to await trial; he packed camp and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the man begged for mercy, and the king interceded for him. Lian Xixian relented slightly and ordered him held for trial—but that night the man broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 俄詔國王歸國，希憲獨行省事。

translations.literal: Soon an edict recalled the king to his domain; Lian Xixian alone conducted branch affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict recalled the king to his domain, and Lian Xixian governed the region alone.

sentences.zh: 朝廷降鈔買馬六千五百，希憲遣買於東州，得羨餘馬千三百。

translations.literal: The court issued paper notes to buy 6,500 horses; Lian Xixian sent to buy in Dongzhou and obtained a surplus of 1,300 horses.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued paper money to purchase 6,500 horses. Lian Xixian bought them in Dongzhou and obtained 1,300 extra.

sentences.zh: 希憲曰：「上之則若自衒。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian said, "If presented upward it would seem self-boasting."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian said, "To present them to the court would look like self-promotion."

sentences.zh: 」即與他郡之不及者，以其直還官。

translations.literal: Immediately he gave them to other prefectures that fell short and returned their value to the government.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the surplus to other districts that had fallen short of their quotas and returned the purchase price to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 長公主及國壻入朝，縱獵郊原，擾民為甚，希憲面諭國壻，欲入奏之。

translations.literal: The eldest princess and imperial sons-in-law entered court and hunted freely in the suburban fields, greatly disturbing the people. Lian Xixian admonished the son-in-law to his face and wished to enter and memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest princess and her sons-in-law came to court and hunted freely in the countryside, greatly disturbing the people. Lian Xixian rebuked the son-in-law to his face and prepared to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 國壻驚愕，入語公主，公主出，飲希憲酒曰：「從者擾民，吾不知也。

translations.literal: The son-in-law was startled, entered and told the princess; the princess came out, offered Lian Xixian wine, saying, "My followers disturbed the people—I did not know."
translations.idiomatic: The son-in-law was alarmed and told the princess. She came out herself, offered Lian Xixian wine, and said, "My attendants disturbed the people—I did not know."

sentences.zh: 請以鈔萬五千貫還斂民之直，幸勿遣使者。

translations.literal: Please accept 15,000 strings of paper notes to repay what was taken from the people—hopefully do not send envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Take 15,000 strings of paper money to repay what was taken from the people, and please do not send an envoy to the court."

sentences.zh: 」自是貴人過者，皆莫敢縱。

translations.literal: From then on, nobles passing through all did not dare indulge.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no noble passing through dared to hunt recklessly again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，右丞阿里海牙下江陵，圖地形上於朝，請命重臣開大府鎮之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Right Chancellor Ali Haiya took Jiangling, submitted a terrain map to court, and requested appointing a senior minister to open a great prefecture to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the right chancellor Ali Haiya captured Jiangling, submitted a map of the terrain to court, and asked that a senior minister be sent to establish a major administrative center there.

sentences.zh: 帝急召希憲還，使行省荊南，賜坐，諭曰：「荊南入我版籍，欲使新附者感恩、未來者向化，宋知我朝有臣如此，亦足以降其心。

translations.literal: The Emperor urgently recalled Lian Xixian, made him pacification commissioner of Jingnan, granted a seat, and instructed: "Jingnan has entered our registers. I wish the newly attached to feel gratitude and those not yet come to turn toward civilization. When Song knows our court has a minister such as this, it is also enough to lower their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai urgently recalled Lian Xixian and appointed him regional commissioner of Jingnan. Granted a seat, he instructed him: "Jingnan is now part of our realm. I want those who have just submitted to feel gratitude and those who have not yet submitted to be drawn to us. When the Song see that our court has a minister like you, that alone will win their hearts."

sentences.zh: 南土卑濕，於卿非宜，今以大事付託，度卿不辭。

translations.literal: The southern land is low and humid—not suitable for you—but now I entrust a great affair; I expect you will not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The south is low and damp and hardly suited to your health, but I entrust you with a great task and expect you will not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」賜田以養居者，馬五十以給從者。

translations.literal: He granted fields to support those dwelling there and fifty horses to supply followers.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him fields to support his household and fifty horses for his retinue.

sentences.zh: 希憲曰：「臣每懼才識淺近，不能勝負大任，何敢辭疾。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian said, "Your servant always fears shallow talent and learning, unable to bear a great charge—how dare I decline on grounds of illness?"
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian said, "I always fear that my talent is too slight for so great a charge—how could I refuse on grounds of illness?"

sentences.zh: 然敢辭新賜。

translations.literal: Yet I dare decline the new grants."
translations.idiomatic: But I must decline the new grants."

sentences.zh: 」復有詔，令希憲承制授三品以下官。

translations.literal: Again there was an edict ordering Lian Xixian by imperial commission to appoint officials of the third rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict authorized Lian Xixian, acting by imperial commission, to appoint officials of the third rank and below.

sentences.zh: 希憲冒暑疾驅以進。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian braved heat and rushed on.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian pressed on through the summer heat without delay.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，阿里海牙率其屬郊迎，望拜塵中，荊人大駭。

translations.literal: On reaching the post, Ali Haiya led his subordinates to welcome at the suburbs; bowing from afar in the dust—the people of Jing were greatly amazed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his post, Ali Haiya led his subordinates out to welcome him at the suburbs, bowing from afar through the dust. The people of Jing were astonished.

sentences.zh: 即日禁剽奪，通商販，興利除害，兵民按堵。

translations.literal: That same day he banned plunder, opened commerce, promoted benefit and removed harm—soldiers and people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he banned looting, reopened trade, promoted what benefited the people and removed what harmed them, and soldiers and civilians alike lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 首錄宋故宣撫、制置二司幕僚能任事者，以備采訪，仍擇二十餘人，隨材授職。

translations.literal: First he registered able Song former xuanfu and zhizhi office staff for investigation and selection; still chose twenty-odd men and assigned posts according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: First he registered capable former staff of the Song xuanfu and zhizhi offices for consideration, then selected more than twenty and assigned them posts according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 左右難之，希憲曰：「今皆國家臣子也，何用致疑。

translations.literal: Those around him objected. Lian Xixian said, "Now all are the state's servitors—why doubt them?"
translations.idiomatic: Those around him objected. Lian Xixian said, "They are all subjects of the state now—why doubt them?"

sentences.zh: 」時宋故官禮謁大府，必廣致珍玩，希憲拒之，且語之曰：「汝等身仍故官，或不次遷擢，當念聖恩，盡力報效。

translations.literal: At the time Song former officials courting the great prefecture always lavished rare treasures; Lian Xixian refused them and told them: "You still bear former titles or may be promoted out of turn—you should remember imperial grace and exert yourselves in repayment."
translations.idiomatic: Former Song officials visiting the regional seat would bring lavish gifts of curios and treasures. Lian Xixian refused them and said, "You still hold your former ranks, or may be promoted out of turn—you should remember the Emperor's grace and serve with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 今所饋者，若皆己物，我取之為非義；

translations.literal: What you now present—if all your own goods, my taking them is unrighteous;
translations.idiomatic: If what you offer is entirely your own property, my taking it would be wrong;

sentences.zh: 一或係官，事同盜竊；

translations.literal: if any ties to government property, the affair equals theft;
translations.idiomatic: if any of it is government property, that is theft;

sentences.zh: 若斂於民，不為無罪。

translations.literal: if extorted from the people, it is not without crime.
translations.idiomatic: if extorted from the people, that is also a crime.

sentences.zh: 宜戒慎之。

translations.literal: You should be vigilant and careful."
translations.idiomatic: Be on your guard."

sentences.zh: 」皆感激謝去。

translations.literal: All were moved and thanked as they left.
translations.idiomatic: They left deeply moved and grateful.

sentences.zh: 令凡俘獲之人，敢殺者，以故殺平民論。

translations.literal: He ordered that whoever among captives dared kill would be judged as deliberate killing of a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that anyone who killed a captive would be prosecuted as having murdered a civilian.

sentences.zh: 為軍士所虜，病而棄之者，許人收養；

translations.literal: Those taken captive by soldiers who were ill and abandoned—people were permitted to adopt them;
translations.idiomatic: Captives taken by soldiers who fell ill and were abandoned might be adopted by others;

sentences.zh: 病愈，故主不得復有。

translations.literal: when illness healed, the former master could not reclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: and once they recovered, their former captors could not reclaim them.

sentences.zh: 立契券質賣妻子者，重其罪，仍沒入其直。

translations.literal: Those who pawned and sold wives and children by contract—he punished them heavily and still confiscated the price.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pawned or sold wives and children under contract were punished severely, and the purchase price was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 先時，江陵城外蓄水扞禦，希憲命決之，得良田數萬畝，以為貧民之業。

translations.literal: Previously outside Jiangling city water was stored to defend against attack; Lian Xixian ordered it released, obtaining tens of thousands of mu of good fields as livelihood for the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Previously a reservoir outside Jiangling had been kept for defense. Lian Xixian ordered it drained, reclaiming tens of thousands of mu of good farmland for the poor.

sentences.zh: 發沙市倉粟之不入官籍者二十萬斛，以賑公安之饑。

translations.literal: He released 200,000 hu of Shashi granary grain not entered in official registers to relieve famine in Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He released 200,000 hu of grain from the Shashi granary that had not been entered in the official registers to relieve famine in Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 大綱既舉，乃曰：「教不可緩也。

translations.literal: The great outline having been raised, he then said, "Teaching cannot be relaxed."
translations.idiomatic: Once the main policies were in place, he said, "Education must not be neglected."

sentences.zh: 」遂大興學，選教官，置經籍，旦日親詣講舍，以厲諸生。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly promoted learning, selected instructors, placed classics, and daily in person went to the lecture hall to encourage students.
translations.idiomatic: He then greatly expanded education, appointed instructors, stocked the libraries with classics, and each day went in person to the lecture hall to encourage the students.

sentences.zh: 西南溪洞，及思、播田、楊二氏，重慶制置趙定應，俱越境請降。

translations.literal: Southwestern stream caves, and the Si, Bo, Tian, and Yang clans, and Chongqing zhizhi Zhao Dingying—all crossed borders to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern tribal territories, the Si, Bo, Tian, and Yang clans, and Zhao Dingying, the Chongqing regional commissioner, all crossed the border to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝曰：「先朝非用兵不可得地，今希憲能令數千百里外越境納土，其治化可見也。

translations.literal: When reported, the Emperor said, "The former court could not obtain territory without using troops—now Lian Xixian can make lands thousands of li away cross borders to yield soil; his governing and transforming power can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Kublai, he said, "The previous regime could not take territory without force—yet Lian Xixian has brought lands thousands of li away to submit across the border. His power to govern and transform is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 」關吏得江陵人私書，不敢發，上之，樞密臣發之帝前，其中有曰：「歸附之初，人不聊生。

translations.literal: Border clerks obtained a private letter from a Jiangling man, did not dare open it, and submitted it upward. Privy Council ministers opened it before the Emperor; therein it said, "At the beginning of submission people could scarcely live."
translations.idiomatic: Border officials seized a private letter from a man in Jiangling but dared not open it and sent it up. Privy Council ministers opened it before Kublai. It read, "When we first submitted, the people could barely survive."

sentences.zh: 皇帝遣廉相出鎮荊南，豈惟人漸德化，昆蟲草木，咸被澤矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Chancellor Lian to govern Jingnan—not only did people gradually receive virtue and transformation; even insects, plants, and trees all received his grace."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Chancellor Lian to govern Jingnan—not only have the people gradually been transformed by virtue; even insects, plants, and trees have all felt his grace."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「希憲不嗜殺人，故能爾也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian does not love killing people—therefore he could be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Lian Xixian has no taste for killing—that is why it is so."

sentences.zh: 希憲疾久不愈，十四年春，近臣董文忠言：「江陵濕熱，如希憲病何？

translations.literal: Lian Xixian's illness long did not heal. In the spring of the fourteenth year, intimate minister Dong Wenzhong said, "Jiangling is damp and hot—what about Lian Xixian's illness?"
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian's illness lingered without recovery. In the spring of the fourteenth year, the intimate minister Dong Wenzhong said, "Jiangling is damp and hot—what will become of Lian Xixian's health?"

sentences.zh: 」即召希憲還，江陵民號泣遮道留之不得，相與畫像建祠。

translations.literal: Immediately Lian Xixian was recalled. Jiangling people wept and blocked the road but could not keep him; together they painted his portrait and built a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian was recalled at once. The people of Jiangling wept and blocked the road, but could not keep him. Together they painted his portrait and built a shrine.

sentences.zh: 希憲還，囊橐蕭然，琴書自隨而已。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian returned with empty bags and cases—only lute and books followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian Xixian returned, his bags were empty—he had brought home only his zither and his books.

sentences.zh: 帝知其貧，特賜白金五千兩、鈔萬貫。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew his poverty and specially granted five thousand taels of white metal and ten thousand strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how poor he was, Kublai specially granted him five thousand taels of silver and ten thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 五月，至上都，太常卿田忠良來問疾，希憲謂曰：「上都，聖上龍飛之地，天下視為根本近聞龍岡遺火，延燒民居，此常事耳，慎勿令妄談地理者惑動上意。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Taichangqing Tian Zhongliang came to inquire after his illness. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Sage ascended as dragon—the realm views it as root and foundation. Recently I heard Dragon Mound had stray fire spreading to burn common dwellings—this is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let those who recklessly discuss geomancy stir the Emperor's mind."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Tian Zhongliang, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, came to inquire after his health. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Emperor rose to power—the realm regards it as the foundation. I have lately heard that stray fire at Dragon Mound spread to burn common dwellings. That is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let geomancers who talk recklessly of fate sway the Emperor's mind."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，果有數輩以徙置都邑事奏，樞密副使張易、中書左丞張文謙與之廷辨，力言不可，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Before long, indeed several people memorialized on relocating the capital city. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian disputed with them in court, strenuously saying it could not be done—the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, several officials did indeed memorialize on moving the capital. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian argued against them in open court, insisting it must not be done. Kublai was displeased.

sentences.zh: 明日，召忠良質其事，忠良以希憲語對，帝曰：「希憲病甚，猶慮及此耶。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned Zhongliang to verify the affair; Zhongliang answered with Lian Xixian's words. The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries to this point?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Kublai summoned Zhongliang to question him about the matter. Zhongliang repeated Lian Xixian's words. Kublai said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries about this?"

sentences.zh: 」其議遂止。

translations.literal: That proposal was thereby stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 詔徵揚州名醫王仲明視希憲疾，既至，希憲服其藥，能杖而起，帝喜謂希憲曰：「卿得良醫，疾向愈矣。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Yangzhou's famous physician Wang Zhongming to view Lian Xixian's illness. When he arrived, Lian Xixian took his medicine and could rise with a staff. The Emperor joyfully told Lian Xixian, "You have obtained a good physician—your illness is nearly healed."
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Wang Zhongming, a famous physician from Yangzhou, to treat Lian Xixian. When he arrived, Lian Xixian took his medicine and was able to rise with a staff. Kublai said joyfully to him, "You have found a fine physician—your illness is nearly cured."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「醫持善藥以療臣疾，苟能戒慎，則誠如聖諭；

translations.literal: He replied, "The physician holds good medicine to treat your servant's illness—if able to be vigilant and careful, then truly as Your Sagely instruction;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The physician has good medicine for my illness. If I can be vigilant and careful, then it will indeed be as Your Majesty says;

sentences.zh: 設或肆惰，良醫何益。

translations.literal: but suppose one indulges idleness—what use is a good physician?"
translations.idiomatic: but if I indulge in idleness, what good is even the finest physician?"

sentences.zh: 」蓋以醫諷諫也。

translations.literal: This was using medicine as indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He was using the physician as a vehicle for indirect remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 會議立門下省，帝曰：「侍中非希憲不可。

translations.literal: At a conference on establishing the Department of Palace Attendants, the Emperor said, "Attendant-in-chief—none but Lian Xixian will do."
translations.idiomatic: At a conference on establishing the Department of Palace Attendants, Kublai said, "For attendant-in-chief, no one but Lian Xixian will do."

sentences.zh: 」遣中使諭旨曰：「鞍馬之任，不以勞卿，坐而論道，時至省中，事有必須執奏，肩輿以入可也。

translations.literal: He sent a palace envoy to convey the order: "Tasks of saddle and horse shall not weary you—sit and discuss the Way; when the time comes go to the department. When affairs must be firmly memorialized, you may enter by sedan chair."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a palace envoy with the order: "You need not trouble yourself with riding duties—sit and discuss policy, and come to the department when needed. When something must be firmly memorialized, you may enter by sedan chair."

sentences.zh: 」希憲附奏曰：「臣疾何足卹。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian attached a memorial saying, "Your servant's illness is nothing worth grieving."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian added a memorial saying, "My illness is nothing worth grieving over."

sentences.zh: 輸忠效力，生平所願。

translations.literal: To offer loyalty and exert strength is life's wish."
translations.idiomatic: To offer loyal service with all my strength is what I have wished for all my life."

sentences.zh: 」皇太子亦遣人諭旨曰：「上命卿領門下省，無憚群小，吾為卿除之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also sent someone to convey the order: "His Majesty commands you to head the Department—do not fear petty men; I will remove them for you."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also sent a messenger with the order: "His Majesty commands you to head the Department of Palace Attendants. Do not fear petty men—I will remove them for you."

sentences.zh: 」竟為阿合馬所沮。

translations.literal: In the end it was obstructed by Ahmad.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Ahmad blocked it.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，賜鈔萬貫，詔復入中書，希憲稱疾篤。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, ten thousand strings of notes were granted; an edict again entered him into the Secretariat—Lian Xixian said his illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year he was granted ten thousand strings of paper money, and an edict recalled him to the Secretariat. Lian Xixian said his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遣侍臣問疾，因問治道，希憲曰：「君天下在用人，用君子則治，用小人則亂。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince sent attending ministers to inquire after his illness and thereby asked about the Way of governing. Lian Xixian said, "Ruling all under Heaven lies in employing people—employ gentlemen and there is order; employ petty men and there is chaos."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent attendants to inquire after his health and asked him about governance. Lian Xixian said, "Ruling the realm depends on whom you employ—employ gentlemen and there is order; employ petty men and there is chaos."

sentences.zh: 臣病雖劇，委之於天。

translations.literal: Your servant's illness, though severe, I entrust to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: As for my own illness, severe though it is, I leave it to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 所甚憂者，大奸專政，群小阿附，誤國害民，病之大者。

translations.literal: What I greatly worry about: a great villain monopolizes government, petty men fawn and attach, harm the state and injure the people—that is the great illness."
translations.idiomatic: What I greatly fear is that a great villain monopolizes power, petty men fawn upon him, and the state is harmed and the people injured—that is the grave illness."

sentences.zh: 殿下宜開聖意，急為屏除，不然，日就沉痾，不可藥矣。

translations.literal: Your Highness should open sagely intent and urgently remove them—otherwise, daily approaching deep affliction, it cannot be cured by medicine."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should open the Emperor's mind and remove them at once—otherwise the realm will sink day by day into mortal illness, beyond any physician's cure."

sentences.zh: 」戒其子曰：「丈夫見義勇為，禍福無預於己，謂皋、夔、稷、契、伊、傅、周、召為不可及，是自棄也。

translations.literal: He admonished his sons: "A man who sees righteousness acts bravely—fortune and misfortune do not concern himself. To say Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, Qi, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, Duke of Zhou, and Duke of Shao are beyond reach is to abandon oneself."
translations.idiomatic: He admonished his sons: "A man who sees what is right acts boldly—fortune and misfortune should not enter his calculations. To say that Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Qi, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao are beyond reach is to abandon yourself."

sentences.zh: 天下事苟無牽制，三代可復也。

translations.literal: If affairs under heaven were not subject to obstruction, the Three Dynasties could be restored.
translations.idiomatic: If nothing held back the affairs of the realm, the golden age of the Three Dynasties could be restored.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「汝讀狄梁公傳乎？

translations.literal: He also said, "Have you read the biography of Duke Liang of Di?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "Have you read the biography of Duke Liang of Di?"

sentences.zh: 梁公有大節，為不肖子所墜，汝輩宜慎之！」

translations.literal: The Duke had great integrity but was brought down by unworthy sons—you should be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke possessed great integrity yet was ruined by unworthy sons—you must take care!"

sentences.zh: 十七年十一月十九夜，有大星隕于正寢之旁，流光照地，久之方滅。

translations.literal: On the night of the nineteenth day of the eleventh month in the seventeenth year, a great star fell beside the main sleeping hall; its streaming light illuminated the ground and only after a long time did it fade.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the nineteenth day of the eleventh month in the seventeenth year, a great star fell beside the main sleeping hall; its streaming light lit the ground and only after a long time faded away.

sentences.zh: 是夕，希憲卒，年五十。

translations.literal: That same night Lian Xixian died at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Lian Xixian died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，贈忠清粹德功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司，追封魏國公，諡文正。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade he was posthumously granted Loyal, Pure, and Refined in Virtue, Meritorious Subject, Grand Tutor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Wei, posthumous title Cultured and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 8 he was posthumously granted Loyal, Pure, and Refined in Virtue, Meritorious Subject, Grand Tutor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Wei with the posthumous title Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 加贈推忠佐理翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、恒陽王，諡如故。

translations.literal: He was further posthumously granted Conveying Loyalty, Assisting in Governance, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hengyang, with the posthumous title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further posthumously granted Conveying Loyalty, Assisting in Governance, Assisting in Fortune, Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grandee of the State with Opening of a Government Office, First Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hengyang, with the posthumous title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子六人：孚，僉遼陽等處行中書事；

translations.literal: He had six sons: Fu, who concurrently conducted Secretariat affairs for the Liaoyang circuit and elsewhere;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Fu, who concurrently administered the Secretariat for the Liaoyang circuit and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 恪，台州路緫管；

translations.literal: Ke, circuit intendant of Taizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Ke, circuit intendant of Taizhou;

sentences.zh: 恂，中書平章政事；

translations.literal: Xun, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 忱，邵武路緫管；

translations.literal: Chen, circuit intendant of Shaowu;
translations.idiomatic: Chen, circuit intendant of Shaowu;

sentences.zh: 恒，御史中丞；

translations.literal: Heng, Vice Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Heng, Vice Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 惇，江西等處行中書省參知政事。

translations.literal: Dun, Vice Director of the Secretariat for Jiangxi and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, Vice Director of the Secretariat for Jiangxi and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 從弟希賢。

translations.literal: His younger cousin was Lian Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger cousin, Lian Xixian.

sentences.zh: 希賢字達甫，一名中都海牙。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian, style Dafu, also known as Zhongdu Haiya.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian, styled Dafu, was also known as Zhongdu Haiya.

sentences.zh: 伯父布魯海牙嘗曰：「是兒剛果，當大吾家。

translations.literal: His uncle Buluhaia once said, "This boy is firm and resolute; he will enlarge our house."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Buluhaia once said, "This boy is firm and resolute; he will bring greatness to our house."

sentences.zh: 」年二十餘，與從兄希憲同侍世祖，出入禁中，小心慎密。

translations.literal: In his twenties he attended the Shizu Emperor together with his elder cousin Lian Xixian, entering and leaving the inner palace with careful discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he served Kublai together with his elder cousin Lian Xixian, moving in and out of the inner palace with careful discretion.

sentences.zh: 至元初，北部王拘殺使者，世祖選使往諭之，廷臣推希賢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan the northern prince detained and killed envoys; the Shizu Emperor chose an envoy to instruct him, and the courtiers recommended Lian Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhiyuan era a northern prince detained and killed envoys; Kublai chose an envoy to instruct him, and the courtiers recommended Lian Xixian.

sentences.zh: 至則布上意，辭旨條暢，王悔謝，為設宴，贈貂裘一襲、白金一笏。

translations.literal: On arrival he conveyed the imperial intent in clear and orderly language; the prince repented and apologized, held a feast for him, and gave him one sable fur coat and one ingot of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he conveyed the imperial intent in clear and orderly speech; the prince repented and apologized, held a feast for him, and gave him a sable fur coat and an ingot of white silver.

sentences.zh: 還奏，帝喜，賜以御膳。

translations.literal: On returning to report, the emperor was pleased and granted him imperial fare.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to report, the emperor was pleased and granted him food from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 尋進中議大夫、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 左丞相伯顏伐宋，既渡江，至元十二年春，授希賢禮部尚書，佩金虎符，與工部侍郎嚴忠範、祕書丞柴紫芝持國書使宋。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Bayan campaigned against Song; after crossing the river, in the spring of the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, Lian Xixian was appointed Minister of Rites, wore the golden tiger tally, and with Vice Minister of Works Yan Zhongfan and Secretariat Director Chai Zizhi bore the state letter as envoy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Bayan campaigned against Song; after crossing the river, in the spring of Zhiyuan 12, Lian Xixian was appointed Minister of Rites, wore the golden tiger tally, and with Vice Minister of Works Yan Zhongfan and Secretariat Director Chai Zizhi bore the state letter as envoy to Song.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌，至廣德軍獨松關，守關者不知為使，襲而殺之。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu of the third month they reached Dusong Pass in the Guangde army; the guards did not know they were envoys and attacked and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu of the third month they reached Dusong Pass in the Guangde army; the guards did not know they were envoys and attacked and killed them.

sentences.zh: 張濡以為己功，受賞，知廣德軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Ru took it as his own achievement, received a reward, and was made administrator of the Guangde army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ru claimed the deed as his own achievement, received a reward, and was made administrator of the Guangde army.

sentences.zh: 明年宋亡，獲張濡殺之，詔遣使護希賢喪歸，後復籍濡家貲付其家。

translations.literal: The next year Song perished; Zhang Ru was captured and executed; an edict ordered envoys to escort Lian Xixian's coffin home, and later the family property seized from Ru was returned to his family.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Song fell; Zhang Ru was captured and executed; an edict ordered envoys to escort Lian Xixian's remains home, and later the property seized from Ru's family was returned to them.

sentences.zh: 希賢死時，年二十九。

translations.literal: When Lian Xixian died he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian was twenty-nine when he died.
